|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

🔵 **`T809` is therefore restated, not defended: the PRIMARY/DERIVED distinction is a real and useful READABILITY property — it marks which row to trust as the origin of a grade — but it is NOT a measure of falsifiability, and no adoption percentage should be built on it.**

## 🆕 `p651` — `2026-11-04` — **🔴 A HEADLINE CLAIM THIS BASE PUBLISHED IN THREE FILES IS FALSIFIED BY A `1.2k★` `MIT` PLATFORM, AND THE MECHANISM IS THE ENUMERATION, NOT THE MEASUREMENTS. 🟢 `649-R4`'s APACHE REGISTER GAINS AN EIGHTH MECHANISM AND ITS FIRST FULLY-EXPLAINED NEGATIVE RESIDUAL. 🔴 A NEW IDENTITY CHANNEL NAMED AFTER THIS BASE PUBLISHED A VERDICT AGAINST THE WRONG ADDRESS.**

### 🔴 `651-R1` — FALSIFIED, and it was this base's most-repeated conclusion: *"there is no permissively-licensed production open source LMS"*

Published in `repos/foundations.md`, `verticals/solutions.md` and `intel/trends.md` **T6**, at **confidence: high**, supported by licence payloads read byte-for-byte across ten platform rows.

[`learningequality/kolibri`](https://github.com/learningequality/kolibri):

| channel | reading `2026-11-04` |
| --- | --- |
| `ls-remote --symref` | 🟢 resolves; real default branch **`develop`**; release lines `release-v0.19.x`, `release-v0.20.x` |
| grant payload (`LICENSE`, `develop`) | 🟢 **`1,097 B`**, title `MIT License`, holder `Copyright (c) 2021 Learning Equality and other contributors` |
| repository page sidebar | 🟢 `MIT license` |
| stars / forks | 🟢 **`1.2k` / `1.0k`** |
| README | *"the offline-first platform for teaching and learning with technology **without requiring the Internet**"* |

🔴 **Every supporting measurement was correct and the conclusion was still wrong.** The ten payloads were read accurately; nine *were* copyleft. The defect is in the **enumeration**: each pass asked "is there a permissive LMS?", populated the comparison set with the institutional LMS field (Moodle, Open edX, Chamilo, ILIAS, Sakai, Frappe, Veo, Gibbon, RosarioSIS, Richie), found it uniformly copyleft, and generalised to *all of open source education*. Kolibri was never a candidate, because it is not an institutional LMS — no enrolment-at-scale, no Moodle-class gradebook, no large third-party plugin ecosystem. 🔵 **The question's framing excluded its own answer.**

🟢 **Corrected claim, stated at the width the evidence supports:** there is no permissive platform **of the Moodle/Open edX class**. There **is** a permissive, adopted, production platform for **offline-first learning delivery**, and it permits a closed derivative.

🔴 **The standing rule this earns, and it is about `∄` claims generally.** A measurement establishes a property of the thing measured. A **"there is no X"** claim is a property of the *search*, and its strength is bounded by the enumeration — never by the number of payloads read inside it. 🔵 This base has a strong instrument for byte-level verification and **no instrument at all for enumeration adequacy**, which is why a universally-quantified claim could sit at `confidence: high` across several passes on ten correct readings. **Registered as `ACTION 651-R1`:** every `∄` claim on a curated shelf must state the enumeration it was taken over, so the next pass can attack the enumeration rather than re-measure the payloads. The three affected files now carry the corrected claim with its boundary named.

🔵 **How it surfaced is itself the method result:** not from a licence census, but from an **EMEA-Africa opportunity search for an offline-first base**. The counter-example was found by a question about *capability*, by someone not looking for a licence. A census structurally cannot find what its own category scheme excludes — `647-C` said the sort key is the filter; `651-R1` says **the category is the filter**, and it is the more expensive of the two.

### 🟢 `651-R2` — `649-R4`'s Apache register: an eighth mechanism, and the first negative residual that is fully explained

`649-R3` closed `648-G` as cohort-specific (`3 of 4` at `11,357 B`); `649-R4` held the register open on `OpenOLAT/OpenOLAT` at `−375`, the first **substantive** deviation. Two further payloads this pass, in opposite directions, and both resolve:

| repo | bytes | Δ canonical | mechanism | recovers? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`openedx/XBlock`](https://github.com/openedx/XBlock) | `11,358` | **`+1`** | 🟢 **one prepended blank line.** `sed '/./,$!d'` yields exactly `11,357` | 🟢 yes — presentation |
| [`ai-shifu/ai-shifu`](https://github.com/ai-shifu/ai-shifu) | `11,342` | **`−15`** | 🟢 **the appendix placeholder is filled in.** Canonical carries `Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]` (`32` ch); this payload carries `Copyright 2024 ai-shifu.com` (`17` ch). `32 − 17 = 15`, exactly | 🔴 no — and it is **correct** |
| [`thm-mni-ii/feedbacksystem`](https://github.com/thm-mni-ii/feedbacksystem) | `10,785` | `−572` | 🟡 appendix in filled short form; `Copyright 2021 Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen` | 🔴 no; not decomposed further this pass |
| [`HKUDS/DeepTutor`](https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepTutor) | `11,408` | `+51` | 🟢 one prepended blank line (`→ 11,407`) plus a `50 B` appended attribution | 🟡 partially |

🔴 **The eighth mechanism matters because it defeats the sign discriminator on the Apache arm.** `647-E` established, for MIT, that the **sign** of the residual is informative: positive means a body anomaly, `−1` means check the last byte. `651-R2` shows the Apache arm does not share that property. `ai-shifu` is a **genuine, unmodified Apache-2.0 grant, correctly applied** — the appendix placeholder substituted with a real copyright line, which is precisely what the appendix instructs a licensor to do — and it reads **`15 B` short**. So on Apache payloads a negative residual can mean *the licensor followed the instructions*, while `649-R4`'s `−375` means the appendix was deleted. 🔵 Same sign, opposite verdicts, and the magnitude alone does not separate them.

🟢 **The decomposition that does separate them, specified for implementation:**
1. strip leading blank lines → recovers all `+1`-class payloads (`XBlock`, `649-R3`'s `edugraph-ontology`);
2. count occurrences of `APPENDIX: How to apply the Apache License` → `0` means deleted (`OpenOLAT` class, substantive);
3. if the appendix is present, extract its `Copyright` line and compare its length against the canonical placeholder's `32` characters → a deficit equal to that difference is **benign substitution** (`ai-shifu` class);
4. only a residual surviving all three is a body anomaly.

🔴 **And a standing hazard, stated plainly:** `openedx/XBlock` is the row every Open edX recommendation in this base is built on — `compose/patterns.md` **P3** exists specifically to put client code inside it. A byte-equality Apache gate over this shelf **fails on that row**, cosmetically. `646-B` warned that an instrument whose failure mode is a plausible positive needs a contradicting control; this is the mirror: an instrument whose failure mode is a plausible **negative** on the base's most load-bearing row.

### 🔴 `651-R3` — OPEN, NEW: the fork notice is an identity channel this base does not read, and it published a verdict against the wrong address

`p650` filed [`kvnloo/tutor-mcp`](https://github.com/kvnloo/tutor-mcp) under "real, and deliberately not filed", with the verdict *"zero stars, zero forks: no adoption, no external review. Watch; do not stake an engagement on it."*

| channel | `kvnloo/tutor-mcp` | [`ArnaudGuiovanna/tutor-mcp`](https://github.com/ArnaudGuiovanna/tutor-mcp) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| licence payload | `MIT`, **`1,073 B`** | `MIT`, **`1,073 B`** — 🔴 identical |
| description string | identical | 🔴 identical |
| `ls-remote --symref` | `main` | `main` |
| stars / forks | `0` / `0` | 🟢 **`96` / `13`** |
| 🔴 repository page, fork notice | 🔴 **"forked from ArnaudGuiovanna/tutor-mcp"** | 🟢 none |

🔴 **Every channel this base measures agreed, which is exactly the failure condition.** The licence payload is byte-identical — necessarily so, since a fork copies it — and so is the description. The **one** channel that distinguishes the pair is the fork notice, and this base does not read it. The published verdict was therefore sound reasoning attached to the wrong object: the project it described has `96` stars and `13` forks.

🟢 **Registered as `ACTION 651-R3`:** when two addresses agree on licence payload bytes **and** description string, treat them as a fork pair and read the fork notice before publishing any adoption verdict. 🔵 Note the asymmetry that makes this cheap — the probe need only run on **collisions**, which are rare, and a collision on payload bytes alone is not enough to trigger it (canonical MIT at `1,073 B` is common; `1,073 B` *and* an identical description is not).

🔴 **Downstream corrections made this pass:** `agents/top.md` files the upstream at `96★` and retains the fork row pointing here; `intel/trends.md` **T9** withdraws the `0`-star datum it used as evidence for the commercial immaturity of knowledge tracing (the claim survives on pyKT `457★` and OATutor `276★`); `compose/patterns.md` withdraws its exclusion of `tutor-mcp` and builds the new **P6** on the upstream.

One search on the project's own name returned the live address immediately. 🟢 **Registered as `ACTION 651-R4`:** a `∄`-by-address finding requires a **name search** before the project is declared gone, not only an address walk — which is `651-R1`'s enumeration rule arriving on the identity channel instead of the category channel. **The same defect twice in one pass, in two different shelves.**

That is the inverse of `609-I` (README grants MIT, links a missing `LICENSE`): there the terms were missing and the claim present; here the terms are present and the attribution dangles. ### 🔴 `651-R5` — OPEN, NEW: resolving the default branch is necessary and **not sufficient**

This base's standing rule is to resolve the default branch with `ls-remote --symref` before cloning. Three rows this pass confirm why (`openeducat_erp` → `19.0`; `rosariosis` → `mobile` among 44 otherwise-version branches; `kolibri` → `develop`; `feedbacksystem` → `dev`). 🔴 A fourth defeats the rule itself:

[`GeminiLight/gen-mentor`](https://github.com/GeminiLight/gen-mentor) — `WWW '25` Industry Track oral, `CC0-1.0`, `136★`. Its default branch **is** `main`, so the rule reports success. But `main` is a **browser-only Next.js application with no server-side database**, and the README states that **the multi-agent Python implementation the paper evaluates is on branch `v0.1-demo`**. Resolving the default therefore yields a demo, not the artefact — and a reproduction attempt against `main` would measure the wrong system entirely while every branch check passed.

🟢 **Registered as `ACTION 651-R5`:** for any row filed on the strength of a paper or a specific capability, resolve the default branch **and** read the README for which branch carries that artefact. `compose/patterns.md` carries the four live cases as a table so the warning sits where someone is about to clone.

### 🔵 `651-R6` — the mandated web legs: nil on the supply arm for a sixteenth pass, but **not nil** on the demand arm

🟢 **Supply arm: nil again.** Global and per-region searches for open source education agents and repos returned candidates this base already holds, plus the novel rows recorded on the trending shelves. No leg produced an adoptable address this base lacked and could file on terms — the sixteenth consecutive effective nil on that arm, consistent with `647-K`.

1. **South Korea's AI Basic Act** (in force `2026-01-22`) names AI for **student assessment in early-childhood, elementary and secondary education** inside its high-impact definition, with administrative fines expected from around `2027-01`. This base characterised APAC as service-specific, labelling-first and voluntary across China, India and Japan — a characterisation that was **incomplete, not merely incomplete in detail**: the region has a binding horizontal statute that names education, and its enforcement edge falls *before* the EU's `2027-12-02`.
2. **LATAM denominators.** UNESCO IESALC with UNU-IAS across ~200 institutions in 19 countries: `87%` use AI, `26%` have a formal strategy, **`55%` have no specific AI budget**. The budget figure changes how an engagement must be *sized*, not just how it is argued.
3. **The Africa gap is located rather than declared** — demand and open-weight activity are documented; African builders ship **proprietary applications on open models**, so there is no open-source stack to adopt.

🔵 **And `651-A` records a fourth kind of yield the scorer has no column for: a leg that returned a plausible, specific, dated regulatory claim which one check falsified, keeping three false statutory deadlines out of `intel/market.md`.** 🟢 **Recommendation revised.** Fifteen passes recommended quarterly cadence on the strength of the supply arm's nil. That recommendation should now be **split**: the supply arm is saturated and quarterly is right; the **demand arm is not saturated** and should keep its per-pass cadence, because regulation moves on statutory dates and this pass found a jurisdiction the base had missed entirely for several months after the statute came into force.

### 🔴 `632-A` — NEW, and it inverts this base's oldest rule: the **bytes** misled and the **metadata** was right

🔵 Since `p611` this base has held that *a curated licence column is not evidence* — measured at `1 of 5`
surviving a byte read on a curated index, then at `68 of 68` reproducing for the platform's own
`license.spdx_id` (`p612`). 🔴 Today the platform field read `LGPL-3.0` for
[`EsupPortail/Esup-Pod`](https://github.com/EsupPortail/Esup-Pod) and this pass's `20`-name ladder returned
**`GPL-3.0`**, from `COPYING` at `35,149 B` with the head title `GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE`.

| File | Bytes | Head title | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 `COPYING` — where the ladder stopped | `35,149 B` | `GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE` | `GPL-3.0`, **wrong** |
| 🟢 `COPYING.LESSER` — absent from the `20`-name set | `7,652 B` | `GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE` | `LGPL-3.0`, matches metadata |

🟢 **Mechanism, and it is structural.** The LGPL is published as a **pair**: the Lesser text plus the GPL text
it incorporates by reference. So `COPYING` in any LGPL project *is* the GPL, and a ladder that reaches it
first is **guaranteed** to mis-grade every LGPL repository — not occasionally, always. 🔵 `611-B` hit the
same mechanism from the opposite direction (every `GPL-2.0` file graded `LGPL`). 🟢 Repaired: `COPYING.LESSER`
and `COPYING.LIB` now rank **above** `COPYING`.
🟡 **The general statement, extending `631-C`/`631-D`:** the grading unit is not a file and not a title — it is
the **file set**. `P631-0` said a payload is a document with scope; `632-A` adds that a grant can be
**split across files**, and reading any one of them alone produces a confident wrong answer.
🔴 OPEN as a rule-boundary question: `622-B` closed the `COPYING.LIB` rung *by refutation* on a different
specimen. `632-A` is a counter-example to that closure's generality, and the two need reconciling.

whole-scope grading.

the hedge *"unresolved"* in bullet `0` (about `101 of 848` backlog addresses) and the subject

carry red cells too — it is the **header of the governing table**. Instrument:
`ingest/p610-census-role.py`. Evidence: `evidence/census-role.2026-11-02-p610.tsv`.

### 🔴 `Gap 555-A` — the platform harvest is not scriptable end-to-end, and `make` must not pretend otherwise

🔴 The field is reachable only through a **tool call**, not a socket a `Makefile` can open:
`urllib` from a `python3 -I` script gets **403**, exactly as `curl` does. 🟢 **Mitigation
shipped:** the harvest is committed to `evidence/` and `platform-channel.py` reads the committed
file, so the **join** is reproducible offline while the **harvest** is attested by its commit.
🔴 **A successor re-harvests; it cannot re-derive.** **Asks:** that no gate be wired to this
channel as if it were offline, and that every platform figure carry its harvest date, because a
stale harvest is indistinguishable from a fresh one once committed.

### 🔴 `Gap 555-B` — `operative-body.py` covers six families, and the five `SUBSTANTIVE` rows may not all be substantive

🔴 The containment vocabulary is `Apache-2.0`, `GPL-2.0`, `GPL-3.0`, `LGPL-3.0`, `AGPL-3.0`,
`MIT`. 🔴 **CC 4.0, BSD-2/3-Clause, `ECL-2.0` and `BUSL-1.1` have no operative-span markers
implemented**, so an artefact carrying a verbatim CC or BSD text reads `SUBSTANTIVE` — *unknown*,
reported as if indistinguishable from *defective*. 🔵 That direction is safe and it is not
free: it may be overstating the substantive count among the 8. **Asks:** add CC-BY-4.0 /
CC-BY-SA-4.0 / CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and BSD-2/3-Clause spans, then re-run the 5 — and report the
`SUBSTANTIVE` band as *"unknown or defective"* until it can tell the two apart.

🔴 **A second, subtler limit found by the controls.** Canonical `LGPL-3.0` classifies as
`GPL-3.0+LGPL-3.0`, because LGPL-3.0 **incorporates** GPL-3.0. 🟢 The module reports both
rather than collapsing, which is correct — but it means **containment can never establish
exclusivity**, only presence.

to be the place other licences are cited, so the same window shape fails there.

constraint: an AGPL dependency in a hosted deliverable reaches network use regardless of an

`Third-Party` / `Bundled` / `Dependencies` sub-heading when deciding the project's own
family, and (b) **reports the bundled families separately and prominently**, because they

### 🔴 `Gap 554-C` — composite grants, and `553-A`'s fix is the direct cause

🔴 [`pupilfirst/pupilfirst`](https://github.com/pupilfirst/pupilfirst)'s `LICENSE` opens
*"Portions of this software are licensed as follows"*, assigns `docs/` to **CC BY-SA 4.0**
and client-side JS to **MIT**, and carries the operative **MIT** text **below** the
12-line title-block window. The instrument reported **CC-BY-4.0** with a spurious
`GRANT-ABRIDGED` flag for a project governed by **MIT**.

🔵 **`553-A`'s fix caused it, and that is the lesson worth more than the patch.** The window
that stopped a licence *citing* another licence from poisoning the family is the same window
that stops this reader reaching a composite file's governing grant. **A window is a bet
about where the answer lives, and these two cases put it in opposite places.**

🟢 **Fixed** — `composite()` detects the carve-out preamble, reports
`COMPOSITE-GRANT-PER-PATH` with the governing family and the carve-outs, and suppresses the
abridgement flag, which a composite file fails by construction. 🟢 **Swept: 1 of 80.**
**Asks:** that any future band declare, in the function that computes it, **which window it
reads and why that window is the right bet** — and that a band whose failure is guaranteed
for a known file shape be suppressed at the source, not explained in prose.

### 🔴 `Gap 554-D` — two errors in four lines, both running in the permissive direction

🔴 **(a)** The family matcher knew only Creative Commons' **canonical titles**
(`Attribution-ShareAlike`), so a file writing the **short form** `CC BY-NC-SA 4.0` matched
nothing and fell through to the bare `CREATIVE COMMONS` arm, reported as plain
**CC-BY-4.0**. 🔴 **(b)** Even in canonical form, `Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike`
hit the **ShareAlike** arm first and returned `CC-BY-SA-4.0`, **silently dropping
NonCommercial** — the single term that decides whether Globant may ship an artefact at all.

🔴 **Both errors make a licence look more permissive than it is**, which is the direction
that reaches a proposal. 🔴 It struck
[`learning-commons-org/evaluators`](https://github.com/learning-commons-org/evaluators),
whose two annotated corpora are **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** behind an **MIT badge**.

🟢 **Fixed** — the modifiers are detected **independently**, in both spellings, and the id
is composed (`CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0`), so `NC` can never be pre-empted by another branch; and
`verdict()` now tests for the **modifier** (`-NC`) rather than for one literal id.
🟢 **Swept: 2 of 80; 78 held byte-identical.** **Asks:** that any vocabulary built from
canonical titles be checked against the **abbreviations the ecosystem actually writes**, and
that a family id never be returned by a branch that can discard a modifier.

### 🔴 `Gap 554-E` — this pass's own instrument, wrong on its first use against a new row

🔴 `doc-channel.py` read the **package manifest** with the **prose** patterns written for
READMEs. A manifest writes a bare SPDX id. `"license": "ISC"` in
[`Zenglian990/AI_Tutor_Release`](https://github.com/Zenglian990/AI_Tutor_Release)'s
`package.json` — beside an **MIT** `LICENSE` and an **MIT** README — matched nothing, and
the row was scored `CHANNELS-AGREE`.

🔴 **The manifest was therefore the weakest reader in a module built to compare readers**,
and every disagreement it alone would have caught was scored as agreement. 🔴 **The
published rate before the fix was a lower bound**, and is republished after it.

🟢 **Fixed** — `manifest_families()` reads an SPDX **expression** first (with `OR` treated
as a consumer's *choice*, not a conflict) and falls back to prose only if that fails.
**Asks:** that a multi-channel instrument be calibrated **per channel**, against a case
known to differ on that channel — calibrating on the README channel told this module
nothing about the manifest one.

`553-A` was **latent and introduced by this pass**, not leaked into published data.

conveying.** 🟢 **Fixed** — the exclusion scan is **gated by family**: an OSI-approved family
is never scanned for non-commercial exclusions, because the OSD forbids them.
🔴 **What remains open:** the scan still finds only exclusions that are **worded**. A
source-available licence that shuts integrators out without using any of the scanned phrases
reads `SOURCE-AVAILABLE-NO-WORDED-EXCLUSION` and is not safe. **Asks:** a second,
non-keyword limb — or an explicit refusal to verdict non-OSI families without a human read.

### 🔴 `Gap 553-C` — the symmetric error to `552-D`, and it struck the only LATAM row

🔴 **Caught on the new verdict's first real use.**
[`juanmoisesd/ai-educational-impact-latin-america-dataset`](https://github.com/juanmoisesd/ai-educational-impact-latin-america-dataset)
carries a 1 259 B CC0 payload whose operative sentence is *Affirmer hereby ... waives,
abandons, and surrenders all of Affirmer's Copyright and Related Rights*. **That is a grant.**
`carried()` called it an assertion, for two reasons that are both typography and neither law:
no CC0 **waiver** verb was on the operative list (it was written from permissive and copyleft
grants, which *permit* where a dedication *waives*), and the payload writes `"AS-IS"` where
the list carried `as is`.

🔴 **Why it is registered and not silently fixed:** `552-D` asked for a verdict separating a
19-byte claim from a dead channel, and got one. **The symmetric error — a real grant filed as
a claim because its vocabulary is not on a hand-written list — is the same defect class with
one sign flipped, and it is worse here, because `NOT-CARRIED` reads as a disqualification.**
It would have struck **the only LATAM-placed artefact in four passes** off the shelf on a
hyphen.

🟢 **Fixed** on three limbs: waiver verbs added; hyphens and smart quotes normalised before
matching; and a **third band**, `GRANT-ABRIDGED`, added — a grant can be **carried and still
incomplete**. **Asks:** that every future verdict list its own false-positive surface in the
function that computes it, as `carried()` now does.

### 🔴 `Gap 553-D` — the new band's own false positive, 40 minutes after the band was added

🔴 `GRANT-ABRIDGED` flagged [`openedx/XBlock`](https://github.com/openedx/XBlock) — a row
already on these shelves carrying **complete** Apache-2.0 at `LICENSE.TXT` (**11 358 B**)
*and* a 545 B `NOTICE.txt` that names the Apache License in its opening lines. The band read
the NOTICE as an abridged grant.

🔵 **The fix is the rule the module already applied to stubs (`542-H`) and failed to apply to
its own new band: resolve over the UNION, not per file.** A family is abridged only if **no**
file of that family reaches canonical size. 🔴 **The lesson is narrower and more useful than
the fix:** writing the union rule in a docstring did not make it apply to the next band added
in the same file. **Asks:** the union rule belongs in one shared helper that every band must
call, not in prose each band is trusted to have read.

🔴 The LATAM row does not agree with itself: `main/LICENSE` carries **CC0-1.0 (abridged)**,
its own `README.md` metadata table states **`License: CC BY 4.0`**, and GitHub's
`license.spdx_id` returns **`NOASSERTION`**. 🔴 **CC0 and CC BY 4.0 are not
interchangeable** — CC BY requires attribution, CC0 waives. A corpus built from this dataset
carries an attribution obligation under one reading and none under the other, **and the
repository asserts both.**

🔵 Compounding it: the omitted CC0 clauses include **s3, the Public License Fallback** — the
provision that makes CC0 operate where a bare waiver is not recognised in law, **which is
most of LATAM's civil-law jurisdictions.** **Asks:** a `GRANT-DISAGREES-WITH-DOCUMENTATION`
verdict that reads the payload, the project's own README and the platform field as three
sources and **reports** disagreement rather than silently resolving it in the payload's
favour.

### 🔴 `Gap 553-F` — the platform's licence field is blind to exactly the grants that decide a deliverable

🔴 Seven addresses read on two channels; GitHub's `license.spdx_id` disagrees with the payload
on **two**, and both are the rows whose licence changes what Globant may do:
`Oriole-FDU/Wisepen` (**BUSL-1.1** → `NOASSERTION`) and the LATAM dataset (**abridged CC0** →
`NOASSERTION`).

🔵 **Structural, not a bug.** The detector matches a canonical corpus and emits `NOASSERTION`
when it cannot match — so it fails for **non-OSI source-available** grants and for
**abridged** ones. 🔴 Those are `552-B` and `553-C`: the two bands this base built verdicts
for *because* they decide shippability. **The platform is most silent where the stakes are
highest.** **Asks:** a standing rule, enforced in `P608`, that the platform licence field is
never used as a discovery filter or a verdict; and a measurement, over a larger sample than
seven, of what share of education repositories reading `NOASSERTION` in fact carry a readable
grant.

### 🔴 `Gap 553-G` — the gate stopped being denied, and what it reported was that it fails

🟢 **The denial run ended.** `p552` recorded `make hooks` as DENIED (`Code from External`) —
*eleven denials in twelve passes*. On `p553` the gate **executed**.

🔴 **And it failed: 48 of 68 gates green, 20 red.**

| RED gate | RED gate | RED gate | RED gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gate-offline` | `recount` | `gate-enumeration` | `gate-tables` |
| `gate-dates` | `gate-shelf-consistency` | `gate-region-headings` | `gate-fold-identity` |
| `gate-alias-canonical` | `gate-author-key` | `gate-census-currency` | `gate-grant-path` |
| `gate-census-union` | `gate-ledger` | `gate-i2-sweep-crosscheck` | `gate-union-currency` |
| `gate-action-answered` | `gate-case-collision` | `gate-promotion-ledger` | `gate-cell-reproduction` |

🟢 **None of the 20 is `p553`'s doing, and that is measured rather than asserted.** The gate
was re-run on a **pristine tree** with this pass's nine page edits stashed: **identical exit
status, identical 48/68, byte-identical RED set.** 🔵 So the red is **pre-existing**, and
twelve passes of denial had been concealing a gate that fails on its own.

🔴 **The second half of this gap is an error in this pass's own first draft, and it is
recorded rather than quietly fixed.** `p553` initially wrote *"`make hooks` RAN AND PASSED —
first gate-attested pass in twelve"* into **all nine pages**. The claim came from reading
`$?` after a pipe:

    make hooks 2>&1 | head -15; echo "exit: $?"     # reports head's status, not make's

🔵 `head` exits `0` whether or not `make` failed, so a failing gate read as a passing one.
🔴 **This is `Gap 546`'s defect class in a new place** — a figure produced by a measurement
whose method was not written down beside it — and it is worse here than a wrong number,
because *"gate-attested"* is the claim on which a successor would trust every other figure in
the pass. 🟢 Corrected in all nine pages before commit; the correction is on the record
because an unlogged correction is how the next pass inherits the same habit.

**Asks, three, in priority order:**

1. 🔴 **Never read a pipeline's `$?` for the status of a non-final command.** Use
   `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, or redirect to a file and check `make`'s own status. This belongs in
   the hooks runner's own documentation, not in a pass's memory.
2. 🔴 **A successor must not read `p552` and earlier as gate-attested.** Eleven of twelve
   passes were DENIED, and the twelfth — this one — is RED. **No pass in this window is
   attested.** The denial was never evidence that the gate would have passed.
3. 🟡 **Triage the 20 red gates by whether they block a shelf claim or only a census figure.**
   🔵 First read of the names suggests two classes: *ledger/census/union/recount* gates, which
   concern this base's self-inventory, and *tables/dates/region-headings/case-collision*
   gates, which concern published page shape. 🔴 The second class is the one that can make a
   shelf row wrong for a reader, and it should be triaged first.

**Registered as:** *"a disposition axis asking — is this artefact worth more as a channel

(`GeminiLight/awesome-ai-llm4education`, **5** novel, **40.0 %**) ranks **sixth of seven**.

absolute threshold, and a general index is large by construction.

read the matches before promoting the channel.** 🔵 Evidence:

reads *"a correction announced in prose is not a correction"*. A gap announced in prose is

### 🔴 `Gap 551-B` — the leak has no measurable size, and the rule stamp does not cover the rules

🔴 **Two parts, both found by `p551` against its own work.**

**(i) The aggregate is dialect-dependent.** `p551`'s first run printed
`MISSING-FROM-REGISTER 125`; a second honest dialect of the same matcher printed **481**.
`worded` (`Gap NNN-X`) misses real registrations — `547-I` sits here **seven times** as a
bare backticked id — while `any_form` over-collects back to `100-A` across id spaces that
are not gaps. 🔵 This is `p546`'s five-rules-five-counts situation and its verdict transfers:
*"nobody can tell"*. **Asks:** a gap-id **grammar**, not a third regex.

**(ii) The revision stamp covers data, not code.**
[`../ingest/rule-revision.py`](../ingest/rule-revision.py) hashes `CANONICAL` + `NOT_A_REPO`
+ `PLACEHOLDER`. It does **not** cover `address-count.py`'s extraction regexes (`LINK_TEXT`,
`PAIR`) or its table-row detection, so a change to either moves every count without moving
the stamp. **Asks:** either hash the extraction source text, or split the rule's code from
its data so the data half is all that varies. 🔵 Stated in the instrument's own docstring
under `WHAT IT DOES NOT DO`.

🔵 **Three design decisions the ask did not specify, each forced by a defect
found while building it:**

1. **It reads a git ref, not the working tree.** Run against the working tree

   how `gate-region-headings` ended up in no target for 45 passes. `CLASS 5`.

   (a deleted page — p495 calls failing to recover one a **loss**) and
   `BACKLOG` (measured in evidence, never filed) are green and carry
   **different instructions**: recover versus promote.
3. 🔴 **`CLASS 6`, found by the gate failing on its own author.** It graded
   `UFPA-LAMIC/EduAcess` as already-held on the strength of one occurrence:
   the fixture in its **own test file**. An instrument that walks
   `compose/code/` indexes its own test data as corpus, and the suites here
   quote real rows deliberately (p392). Test files are not corpus.

**First real use, which is the number that justified it:** 20 candidates from
the mandated legs, **20 already held** (2 `FILED`, 3 `HISTORY`, 15 intel
claims). Evidence:
[`../evidence/restated-presence-grade.2026-10-30-p541.tsv`](../evidence/restated-presence-grade.2026-10-30-p541.tsv).

### 🔴 Gaps `p541` registers

- 🔴 **`Gap 541-A` — nothing on this base catches a restated ANALYSIS, and
  `540-A`'s gate cannot be extended to.** `p541` built the restated-presence
  gate and then **drafted a restated presence as its own headline**: it
  reported "19 of 37 `UNKNOWN` are a recording artefact" when `p540` had
  already resolved all 37 into twelve dialects, in prose, on
  [`../agents/trending.md`](../agents/trending.md). The gate graded every
  address involved as already-held and that was *correct and useless* — the
  restatement was of a **conclusion**, not an address. 🔵 **Wire it on
  CLAIMS:** a pass's headline assertions carry numbers and named entities;
  grade each headline against the last N passes' headlines for an assertion
  over the same entity set, and require an explicit "this restates `pNNN`"
  or a stated delta. `gate-prose-claims` (p495) already parses load-bearing
  claims — this is the same machinery pointed at the current pass's own
  output rather than at losses. **Highest-value gate change available**, for
  exactly the reason `540-A` was: it audits the base's self-knowledge from
  the side that is still blind.
- 🔴 **`Gap 541-B` — an evidence TSV may contradict the prose that resolved
  it, and nothing notices.** `backlog-gated-slice2.2026-10-30-p540.tsv`
  carries `UNKNOWN` for all 37 rows; p540's page resolved them. A successor
  reading the TSV (as `p541` did) gets a different answer from one reading the
  page, and the TSV is the machine-readable half. 🔵 **Fix:** when a pass
  resolves rows an evidence file records as unresolved, it must either rewrite
  the file or emit a superseding one, and a gate should fail when a curated
  page's prose names a verdict its own cited evidence contradicts. Cheap: both
  artefacts are already in the tree and the join key is the address.
- 🔴 **`Gap 541-C` — this base has TWO grant classifiers and they do not share
  a title table.** [`ingest/backlog-gate.py`](../ingest/backlog-gate.py)'s
  `spdx_of` (substring, carries Portuguese, no Eclipse) and
  [`compose/code/p228-shelf-gate/classify_grant.py`](../compose/code/p228-shelf-gate/classify_grant.py)
  (positional earliest-title, carries EPL and EUPL-1.2, no Portuguese)
  disagreed on **2 of 37** and agree only by coincidence elsewhere.
  🔵 **Fix:** one table, imported by both, with the union of what each
  currently knows **plus `bespoke_guard` in front**. 🔴 Do not merge them
  without the guard — see `540-B` above.
- 🟡 **`Gap 541-D` — the supply census should be run in the client's language,
  and this base has only ever run it in two.** English returned **0 new of 5**;
  Spanish and Portuguese returned **8 new of 10**. The sector's other large
  non-English publishing populations — **Mandarin, Hindi, Bahasa Indonesia,
  Arabic, French** — have never been queried on this base, and APAC supply is
  where the source-available licences concentrate. 🔵 **Measure before
  assuming:** run one leg per language and report the new-address rate, so the
  next pass knows whether the Spanish/Portuguese result generalises or is
  specific to Iberian-Latin American open-source culture.
- 🟡 **`Gap 541-E` — the EUPL version is load-bearing and this base knows one
  of them.** Six of seven `opetushallitus` notices say **EUPL 1.1**, one says
  **1.2**, and the only EUPL title either classifier carries is 1.2. The
  obligations differ, and the version appears **only in the notice** because
  the text is not reproduced. 🔵 **Fix:** carry EUPL 1.1 and 1.2 separately,
  and have `by_reference()`'s captured version reach the shelf cell rather
  than being flattened to "EUPL".
- 🔴 **`Gap 541-F` — four agent rows filed this pass carry 0 stars and 0
  forks, and this base has no fitness floor.** `p541` shelved
  `cjescudero/asistente-docente`, `UFPA-LAMIC/EduAcess`,
  `asistente-docente-sin-conexion` and `TeachGPT` for their **grant and
  shape**, said so in every row, and that is still a judgement call made
  pass by pass. 🔵 **Decide it once:** either a stated floor below which an
  artefact is recorded as a *signal* rather than shelved as an *agent*, or an
  explicit "grant and shape qualify regardless of traction" rule written into
  the shelf's own contract. `p534`'s fitness axis is the place it belongs.
  🔴 Until it exists, a reader cannot tell a 0★ row that was judged from a
  0★ row that was not.

### 🟡 `Gap 534-H` — three capabilities this base records as blocked are **not** blocked, and nobody re-tested them

**The defect, and it is the most expensive one `p534` found.** Three standing
claims in this base's own prose were refuted this pass, each by a single
cheap test:

| Claim, as written here | Passes carried | Measured at `p534` |
|---|---|---|
| *"`github.com` and `api.github.com` are both HTTP 403 through this session's proxy"* | `p532`, `p533` | 🔴 **Half wrong.** `github.com` HTML is **200 through WebFetch** — org listings with stars and licences, which is the whole of `Gap 533-A`'s remedy. `api.github.com` is genuinely closed |
| *"no gate reads table boundaries"* | registered and retracted **within this pass** | 🔴 **Wrong.** `make gate-tables` has graded `cross-table-blank` since `p277` |
| *"`make hooks` was DENIED (`Code from External`) — ten denials in eleven passes"* | `p455` and around it | 🟡 **Not denied at `p534`.** It ran, and gates reported green as they went |

🔵 **The pattern is one failure mode, not three incidents:** a negative result
about the *environment* was written into prose, and prose is not re-tested. A
licence cell gets re-read every pass; *"that channel is blocked"* never does,
so it hardens into a constraint that silently shapes every later pass's plan —
`Gap 533-A` priced its own remedy at *"one API call per org"* and therefore
deferred it, when the capability was a single request away.

**Remedy, scoped.** A standing **capability probe** — one script, four or five
assertions (raw 200, `github.com` HTML via each channel, `api.github.com`, `make
hooks` runnable), run at the **start** of every pass, output to
`evidence/capabilities.<date>-<pass>.tsv`, and **no prose claim about a blocked
channel permitted without a dated row in it**. 🔵 **Cost:** minutes per pass.
🔴 **Benefit, measured:** this pass's largest find (`mitodl/learn-ai`) was
unreachable under the old claim and trivially reachable once it was tested.

### 🟡 `Gap 534-I` — the claim register can demand a sentence this base has refuted

**The defect.** `make gate-prose-claims` holds `NO-PERMISSIVE-PLATFORM` and
greps [`../repos/foundations.md`](../repos/foundations.md) for
**"No permissive education platform exists."** 🔴 **That sentence is false**:
this base files [`oppia/oppia`](https://github.com/oppia/oppia) (**Apache-2.0**,
7.0k★), [`OpenOLAT/OpenOLAT`](https://github.com/OpenOLAT/OpenOLAT)
(**Apache-2.0**), [`learningequality/kolibri`](https://github.com/learningequality/kolibri)
(**MIT**) and [`sakaiproject/sakai`](https://github.com/sakaiproject/sakai)
(**ECL-2.0**). 🔵 So the register, whose whole purpose is to stop a true claim
being deleted silently, now **pressures a future pass into re-asserting a false
one** — and the cheapest way to make that gate green is to write the falsehood
back.

🟢 **How `p534` discharged it, and why that is the right shape.** The claim is
recorded in the owing file as a **dated retraction** naming the four addresses
that killed it. The gate goes green because the claim's *fate* is in the file —
which is what `p494` actually established ("a deleted claim is
indistinguishable from coverage"), not that the claim must still hold.

**Remedy, scoped.** The register needs a **status** column — `LIVE` /
`RETIRED` / `CORRECTED` — so a retired claim is checked for its *retraction*
rather than its assertion. 🔵 **Cost:** one column, plus a pass over the 30-odd
register rows to classify them. 🔴 **Until then, a green
`gate-prose-claims` means "the claim's fate is recorded", not "the claim is
true", and no one should read it as the latter.**

### 🟡 `Gap 534-J` — `recount`'s anchors point at a file layout that no longer exists

**The defect.** `make recount` reports **`STALE=0, NO-ANCHOR=5 of 5`**. 🟢 **No
count it checks is wrong** — but all five anchors target sentences that have been
removed: an `agents/top.md` **"MCP section"** with its own lead sentence and
table, an `N permissive rows` sentence in a structurally-bounded build-on tier,
and trends **`T21`** and **`T24`** on a file that now holds twenty numbered
trends under different headings.

🔵 **Why this is worse than a stale number.** A `STALE` finding says a published
count disagrees with a measurement. A `NO-ANCHOR` finding says **the gate has
stopped checking anything at all** — five counts that were once pinned are now
unpinned, silently, and the gate's own report is the only place that says so.
🔴 The same failure shape as `Gap 534-H`: an instrument degraded into a no-op
and nothing re-tested it.

**Remedy, scoped.** For each of the five: either re-point the anchor at the
sentence that now carries the count, or re-measure and restore the sentence.
🔵 **Cost:** one pass, offline — the counts are all derivable from the shelves
themselves. 🔴 **Do not "fix" it by deleting the register rows**, which is the
move that produced `Gap 534-I`.

### 🔴 The finding `531-A` did not ask for: `p531`'s fold reintroduced the defect it diagnosed

`p531` widened the matcher to fold `[Pp]ass\s+N` after finding that a
case-sensitive `\bPass\s+` had missed a lower-case `pass 277` and attributed that
section to a `` `p276` `` **cited in the same title**. 🔴 **The fold then does the
same thing in a different dialect:**

```
## 2026-10-07 — twenty-ninth pass: … the shared classifier still carried
   every defect pass 28 had just fixed in the other one
      ^ SELF-ID (an English ordinal word)        ^ A CITATION
```

The section's own number is **a word**; the only numeric `pass N` in the title
belongs to a *different* pass. Four headings are mis-read this way
(`twenty-ninth`→28, `twenty-fifth`→24, `fortieth`→39, and a second
`twenty-ninth`→28).

🔴 **And the larger half: a whole dialect neither matcher ever saw.** This base
writes **153** `##` headings with an ordinal-word id —
`## 🟢 Seventieth pass, 2026-10-09 — …`,
`## 🟢 Hundred-and-twenty-fourth pass, 2026-10-11 — …`,
`## 2026-10-07 — forty-third pass: …`. Neither the `p530` nor the `p531` matcher
resolves any of them, so **those sections never reset the pass pointer** and
every address first described in them was attributed to whatever recognised
heading sat above.

🔵 **Why that is the whole early history.** The ordinal dialect is how passes
**1–~70** and the `Hundred-and-*` run were written. So the region of the corpus
that was invisible is precisely the oldest one — which is why the correction
moves `first_seen_pass` *older* by a mean of 50.5 passes and a maximum of 107.
Hand-verified, one address end to end:
`huggingface/smolagents`'s oldest mention is `agents/trending.md:45278`,
governed by `## 2026-10-06 — second pass: licence sweep of the education MCP
shelf` at line 45152 — **`p2`**, recorded until today as **`p109`**.

**Measured over the same 1 532 candidate `##` headings** (census:
[`../evidence/matcher-dialects.2026-10-29-p532.tsv`](../evidence/matcher-dialects.2026-10-29-p532.tsv)):

| Matcher | Headings resolved | Unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| `p530` (case-sensitive) | 1 129 | 403 |
| `p531` (case-folded) | 1 343 | 189 |
| 🟢 **`p532` (positional)** | **1 474** | **58** |

🟢 **The rule that replaces both, and it is positional rather than lexical.** A
heading holds two kinds of number — its own id and a pass it cites — and every
matcher so far searched the whole line and took the first hit. This base writes
`<id/date segment> — <id/date segment> — <title>`, and **the id is always in a
leading segment**. So: split on the em-dash, cut each segment at its first
colon, and take the first segment that yields a token; read the ordinal words,
including `Hundred-and-twenty-fourth`; and accept a bare `pN` only when it is a
segment *on its own*. Single-sourced in
[`../ingest/pass_section.py`](../ingest/pass_section.py), consumed by both
`address-ledger.py` and the new queue — two matchers in two files is how `p531`'s
fix reached one consumer and not the other.

🟢 **The 58 that remain unresolved are correctly declined,** and were read one by
one: `P125-A`-style **gap registrations** (upper-case `P` is the proposal
namespace — `p531`'s own `C1` established that the case of one letter separates
two namespaces), `ACTION XX` blocks, gap roll-ups, and date-only headings such as
`## 2026-10-06` that carry no id at all. 🔵 Both earlier matchers resolved
`## 🔴 🆕 \`P125-A\` — … p124 read by hand` to **p124**, a number that heading
merely cites.

**Ask 2 — `--archives` re-run.** 349 → **286** archive-only addresses: **63
removed, 0 added**.

| | p531 | p532 |
|---|---|---|
| Archive addresses indexed | — | 2 973 (71 files) |
| Candidates, URL channel | — | 527 |
| Suppressed by the bare-slug channel | — | 241 |
| 🟢 **ARCHIVE-ONLY (both channels)** | 349 | **286** |

🟢 **The direction is the right one and it is attributable:** `p531` filed 29
addresses and wrote up others in its trending sections, so 63 of the 349 are now
live. The drop channel shrinking is `p531`'s promotion work becoming measurable.

**Ask 3 — re-bless the ratchet.** 🔴 **NOT DONE, and the reason is the same wall
`p531` hit.** See the attestation below.

🔵 **And the failure has a structural cause worth writing down, because it tells a
successor not to retry this shape.** In a **single-industry** KB the industry's
vocabulary is *ambient*: this base discusses `vllm`, `litellm`, `dspy`,
`llama_index` and `ragflow` in sentences about tutors, courses and students, so

general-infra addresses were called education on prose alone. 🔴 **A
subject filter for this channel must read a repo-side field — `topics`, or the
repository's own description — never a base-side one.** The name-only arm is the
honest fallback: it is precise (0.889) and it misses more than half.

(`open-spaced-repetition/fsrs.js`, `viendinhcom/supermemo`) plus
`alterem/knowledge-grab`; tuning the keyword list on them would be fitting to the
test set, so it was not done.

1. ⛔ **The `make` target truncated its own measurement.** The recipe piped the
   script through **`| head -40`**. The script emits **10 362 rows**, so the
   target reported **40 — 0.4%** — and because snapshots are walked in sorted
   order, the surviving 40 were **always the oldest snapshot**. Worse: `head`
   closing the pipe killed the script on **`BrokenPipeError` before it printed
   its own totals**, so the target produced a traceback and *no summary at all*.
   🟢 Rows now go to [`../evidence/archive-drops.tsv`](../evidence/archive-drops.tsv)
   and the summary is printed. 🔵 **A measurement target that truncates is worse
   than one that fails**, because the truncated number looks like an answer.
2. ⛔ **`MAP` silently skipped the newest snapshot.** It mapped only the
   hyphenated basenames (`agents-top.md`, …). The newest tree,
   `2026-10-27-p490-pre-rewrite`, stores the same files under **plain**
   basenames (`top.md`, `foundations.md`, …), so `MAP.get(base)` returned `None`
   and `continue` dropped **six files** — while the `if not read` guard stayed
   satisfied by the older snapshots. 🟢 Both spellings now accepted; that
   snapshot alone contributes **1 738 rows**. **read=70 of 71 files, 13 of 13
   snapshots.**

### 🔴 Registered this pass

**`Gap 525-A` — `ingest/probe-grant.sh`'s correctness depends on an undocumented accident.**
Its GNU branches are right only because their patterns are UPPERCASE and bash `case` is
case-sensitive, so they match a title block and skip a mixed-case preamble cross-reference.
`oat-sa/tao-core`'s GPLv2 contains *"GNU Lesser General Public License"* — verified today at
`dabc1c180e9f`. **Action:** replace `spdx_of()` per `P544`, and until then add a comment saying the
case-sensitivity is load-bearing. **Do not add `shopt -s nocasematch`.**
🔵 *Not* merely theoretical: the same function already mis-grades `PageLM`, `cn-math-taxonomy` and
`advisingapp` through the sentence-matching half of the same design.

**`Gap 525-B` — `p490`'s "anchor on the title block" is really "anchor on the first 200 bytes", and
inside that window a declaration and a cross-reference are indistinguishable.**
Live example found this pass: `openeducat/openeducat_erp`'s `LICENSE` (`8 241` B,
`sha256₁₆ 528f84036800168d`, ref **`19.0`** @ `46a5d7d40082`) carries **no licence title line** and
instead declares, inside the first 200 bytes, *"published under the GNU LESSER GENERAL PUBLIC
LICENSE, Version 3 (LGPLv3)"*. 🟢 Both readers grade it correctly **off a declaration sentence**.
🔴 A payload that names a *sibling* licence that early would be graded wrong. **Action:** when the
200-byte window contains a family token but no line that is *only* a licence title, emit the family
with `confidence = declaration`, not `title-attested`. No live row exhibits the failing case today,
so this is named, not patched.

**`Gap 525-C` — a 4,392★ MIT asset was 368 days stale and reachable from this base's own shelf row
the whole time.** `panaversity/learn-agentic-ai`'s mainline last moved `2025-10-26`; the same
owner's `panaversity/ksor` has been a shelf row for passes. 🔴 Worse than `fsrs4anki`'s 340 days,
the staleness `p523` built an instrument for. **Action:** run `p523`'s code-vs-docs liveness check
over **owner-adjacent** addresses of every shelf row, not just the rows.

**`Gap 525-D` — a sibling address was taken from a README and never probed.**
`ankimcp/anki-mcp-server-addon` is named in `repos/trending.md` `p525` from
`ankimcp/anki-mcp-server`'s README at `e0e347f7f399`. **Its grant, HEAD and liveness are unread.**

Their findings were written as prose under *"Declared gaps"*, which cannot be closed, cannot be carried and cannot be counted. 🟢 FOUR GAPS CLOSED WITH CONTENT (`488-K`, `488-X`, `488-J`, `488-P`), 🔴 ONE GAP'S REQUESTED ACTION REFUSED AND THE ROW RE-GRADED INSTEAD (`488-L`), 🔴 ONE PUBLISHED TREND WITHDRAWN (`T17`), 🟢 ONE PRIOR WARNING CONFIRMED BY INSTANCE (`489-J`), five of `p497`'s prose gaps given IDs, and ten registered.**

🔵 **`gate-register-currency` — measured and FAILED.** `Gap 473-F`'s check: the register's newest
section must be `p(N-1)` before a pass writes `pN`. 🔴 **Measured: `p488`. Expected: `p497`. Fail,
by ten passes.** 🟢 `p498` writes **nine shelves including this one**.

🔴 **But the diagnosis changes.** `p488` read the failure as a copying failure — gaps registered on
shelves, never mirrored here. 🔴 **This pass measured it instead of assuming it:**

| pass | numbered gap IDs of its own, anywhere on the eight shelves |
|---|---|
| `p489` | 🟢 **4** (`489-I`, `489-J`, `489-K`, `489-L`, on [`repos/trending.md`](../repos/trending.md)) |
| `p490` – `p497` | 🔴 **0. Each.** Eight consecutive passes. |

🔵 **So the register was not starved of nine passes of gaps; eight passes stopped producing
registrable gaps.** Their *"Declared gaps — searched this pass, nothing found"* sections carry real
content — unlicensed LATAM repositories, an unverifiable search hit, an eighth pass with no
permissive tutoring evaluator — but **without an ID, a gap cannot be closed, cannot be carried
forward and cannot be counted against a later pass.** 🔴 That is a worse defect than a copying
failure, and it is invisible to `Gap 473-F`'s check, which measures only *this file's* newest
heading.

🔵 **The contract needs a second clause, and this pass proposes it:** a pass that writes a
*"Declared gaps"* section **must** give each item an ID of the form `Gap <pass>-<letter>`. A prose
gap is a note; an identified gap is a debt. 🟢 Registered below as `Gap 498-K`.

🔴 **One instrument defect of this pass's own, caught and reported rather than quietly fixed.** The
first grant-probe run terminated silently after **22 of 76 rows** with exit code 0. Cause:
`git clone` and `git ls-remote` **consume the loop's stdin**, so the `while read` loop ran out of
input and the script exited cleanly having skipped 54 rows. 🔴 **A truncated run that exits 0 and
writes a plausible 22-row file is indistinguishable from a complete one** unless the row count is
checked against the input. Fixed by reading the list on file descriptor 3. 🔵 The lesson for any
future pass that iterates repositories in shell: **compare output rows to input rows before
believing the result.** Registered as `Gap 498-L`.

### 🆕 `Gap 445-H` — **`gate-promotion-ledger` is DECLARED RED, and the cause is `Gap 421-C` firing live on this base's own tool path**

🔴 **Red on arrival, measured not asserted.** Re-run against `ed86a96` (`p444`'s commit) with
this pass's writes stashed, the gate reports the identical finding at the identical subject:

```
C1-UNADJUDICATED   lib/measure   agents/trending.md:151 claims promotion; no ledger row
```

After `p445`'s prepend the same sentence sits at `agents/trending.md:373`. 🔴 **So this is
`p444`'s unadjudicated claim — the FOURTH gate `p444` left red** (with
`gate-register-currency`, `gate-census-currency` and `gate-union-currency`), and `p445`
inherited it.

🔵 **The cause is not a missing ledger row. It is a parser reading this repository's own file
path as a GitHub address.** `p444`'s sentence is *"Promoted to `repos/foundations.md` — the 8
permissive rows, every cell built by `lib/measure` this hour"*. `claims.py::slugs_in` takes a
backticked `a/b` as a slug unless it ends in a known file extension:

```python
if re.search(r"\.(md|tsv|json|sh|py|txt|xml|ts|yml|yaml)$", s):
    continue
out.append(s)
```

🔴 **`lib/measure` has no extension**, so this base's own measurement tool is parsed as a
promoted repository. 🟢 **This is exactly `Gap 421-C`, which has carried the remedy for 24
passes** — *"the rule needs a this-repository's-own-paths arm, or every consumer must anchor on
`github.com/` as `p348` does"* — and `Gap 421-C` recorded it as **LATENT on both live
channels**. 🔴 **It is no longer latent. This is its first live firing, on a blocking gate.**

### 🔴 Why `p445` declared it rather than fixed it

🔵 The fix is one arm in `claims.py::slugs_in`, and it was deliberately **not** applied. Three
reasons, each a rule this base already wrote:

1. 🔴 **`claims.py` is shared by `p434-promotion-gate`, `p435-promotion-sweep` and
   `p436-promotion-ledger`.** Narrowing `slugs_in` moves the derived claim population
   (**267**) and can move `PROMO_RATCHET = 148`, a figure quoted across prior sections.
2. 🔴 **A change that REDUCES the claim population to get a gate green is indistinguishable,
   from the outside, from loosening a control** — which `p387-G` forbids. It needs its own
   pass, its own controls and its own before/after denominators, not a late side-effect of an
   unattended run.
3. 🔴 **Editing `p444`'s prose to remove the backticked path would be retro-editing** — the
   `dated-by-measurement` convention forbids it, and it would hide the parser defect rather
   than record it.

🟢 **So it is declared, in the open, under a pass number, which is the only sanctioned way to
carry a red** (`p423`): `DECLARED_RED = gate-census-union gate-promotion-ledger`.

🟢 **Prescription, and it is now a sharp one rather than `Gap 421-C`'s general note.** Add the
own-paths arm to `claims.py::slugs_in` — reject a backticked `a/b` whose first segment is one
of this repository's own directories (`lib`, `compose`, `evidence`, `agents`, `repos`, `intel`,
`verticals`, `scratchpad`, `ingest`, `archive`, `scripts`, `bin`) — then **publish the
before/after claim count and ratchet**, pin `lib/measure` as a negative control in
`test_ledger.py`, and re-run all three promotion gates. 🔵 `p444`'s sentence is a ready-made
fixture: it must yield **0** claims, not 1.

### 🟢 `Gap 440-A` — **CLOSED for BSD**, and the gap was wrong twice. MPL and EPL re-registered below

🟢 **Bought to the gap's own stopping rule** — *"BSD first — it is the only one of the three
with a row on a build-on shelf."* Profiles `BSD-2` and `BSD-3` added to
`compose/code/p439-grant-presence/grant_presence.py`, with `resolve_bsd_variant()` and a
`VARIANT_FAMILIES` hook kept apart from `VERSIONED_FAMILIES` because the resolution **method**
differs. `GRANT-UNCALIBRATED` on the BSD slice falls 🟢 **14 → 3**; whole corpus
**39/218 → 29/228** (MPL 9 · LGPL 8 · EPL 9 · BSD 3). The suite is **87 controls**, up from 46.

🔴 **Correction 1 — the gap's prescribed METHOD was unsound.** It asked for the variant
*"resolved from the clause structure, not from the length"*. BSD-2 and BSD-3 are separated by
exactly one piece of text — the non-endorsement clause — which is **also a clause the
instrument grades**. Resolve the variant from it and a **BSD-3 truncated at that clause**
resolves as a BSD-2, is graded against BSD-2's seven clauses and returns `GRANT-PRESENT`:
a false pass on the precise shape the instrument exists to catch. 🟢 **What is sound is the
asymmetry** — presence of the discriminator is proof, absence is ambiguous — so the variant
is resolved from the payload's own **declaration** (the title line, the only BSD signal
independent of the graded clauses), the structural arm may answer only in the direction that
cannot be wrong, and everything else declines. `C26` keeps the refuted alternative
reproducible; mutating the resolver back to the prescription turns **8** controls red.

🔴 **Correction 2 — the gap's DENOMINATOR was 27 % high.** It enumerated *"BSD 14"*. Three of
those fourteen are **KB markdown tables** naming a licence in a cell (`md-form4-italic.md`,
`md-shortname-binding.md`, `md-page-said-header.md`), not licence payloads. The real count was
**11**. `p310`'s rule again, and they are named in `grade_bsd.py` rather than filtered by a
byte floor.

🔴 **Correction 3 — the row the gap named could not have been screened by a BSD profile at
all.** [`Open-TutorAi/open-tutor-ai-CE`](https://github.com/Open-TutorAi/open-tutor-ai-CE)
carries **no title line**, so `bespoke_census.titled_family()` — which answers from the title
by construction — returns `None` and no clause profile is reached. **5 of the 12 live BSD
payloads this base publishes are shaped that way, 4 of them complete BSD-3 grants.** 🟢 The
remedy is `--family`, which lets the hardened owner's answer (`lib/license_family.sh`,
which said `BSD` for all five) be passed in; `P171` forbids re-answering the family here.
All 12 are now graded: 🟢 **11 `GRANT-PRESENT`**.

🟡 **The remainder of `Gap 440-A` stands: MPL (9) and EPL (9), to be bought together.** 🔵 And
`p441` adds a stopping rule the gap did not have: **ask what each family DECLARES that is
independent of the clauses being graded, before writing the profile.** MPL-2.0 declares its
version in its own text (like GPL); EPL-1.0 and EPL-2.0 differ materially and EPL has a
standing registration against a different instrument (`Gap 396-E`), so whichever pass buys it
should close both.

### 🔴 `Gap 441-A` — **OPEN, and it is in the shared library rather than in one caller.** `lib/probe_payload.sh` takes the FIRST filename-ladder hit, and `Gap 393-F` already forbade guessing filenames

is an R package: `DESCRIPTION` reads `License: BSD_3_clause + file LICENSE`, so `LICENSE`

`evidence/verified-repos.2026-10-22-p394.tsv:13` records the three-file shape,
**tree-enumerated per `Gap 393-F`**, and `LICENSE.md` re-read at the pinned commit `693b3df`

🟡 **Realised damage NIL** — no published row was graded from a stub, because `p394` read the

### 🔵 `Gap 441-B` — **OPEN and deliberately unbought.** BSD-0 and BSD-4 are RECOGNISED and UNPROFILED, because this tree has zero payloads of either

🟢 `resolve_bsd_variant()` answers `BSD-0` and `BSD-4` from their declarations, and neither
has a clause profile, so such a payload grades `GRANT-UNCALIBRATED` instead of being measured
against a neighbour's clauses. 🔴 **Writing the profiles would mean taking the clauses from a
licence's reputation rather than from a measured corpus** — exactly what `p440`'s GPL group
was careful not to do. 0BSD grants with **no retention condition at all** (its operative
sentence is ISC-shaped) and BSD-4 adds the advertising clause; neither is approximated by
BSD-2. `C33` pins the decision.

🔵 **Priced**: cheap, but only once supply exists. **Stopping rule: do not buy it until a
0BSD or BSD-4 payload is on this tree** — and then calibrate on that payload, not on the
canonical text.

### 🔴 `Gap 441-C` — **OPEN.** A payload carrying ZERO clauses of ANY BSD variant is unambiguous, and the instrument still declines on it

🔴 **The measurement.** `ucbds-infra/ottr`'s 108 B stub carries **none** of BSD-2's seven
clauses and no variant declaration, so `resolve_bsd_variant()` returns `None` and the verdict
is `GRANT-UNCALIBRATED` — *"not judged"* for a payload that plainly grants nothing. The
correct answer is `GRANT-TRUNCATED`.

🟡 **The sound-looking tightening is not sound.** *"If the payload satisfies NO candidate BSD
profile then no variant is complete, so TRUNCATED"* holds for BSD-2 and BSD-3 — and 🔴 **fails
for 0BSD**, whose complete text contains none of those seven clauses. An **untitled 0BSD**
payload would be condemned. 🔵 So the tightening requires asserting that untitled 0BSD
payloads do not occur, which is a claim about future supply and not a property of any text.

🟢 **The buildable version**: ask first whether 0BSD's own operative sentence
(`permission to use, copy, modify, and/or distribute … with or without fee`) is present, and
only then apply the intersection test. 🔵 That sentence is also **ISC's**, so the question
touches the family classifier's boundary and belongs in a pass of its own, with
`lib/licence_identity.py` as the owner. **Priced: one pass. Stopping rule: only after
`Gap 441-A`** — a probe that reads the wrong file produces far more wrong verdicts than a
decline on the right one.

### 🔴 `Gap 440-B` — **OPEN, and it needs a VERDICT rather than a profile.** LGPL-3.0 incorporates GPL-3.0 by design, so "by reference" is the wrong answer about it

🔴 **The measurement.** On this base's **7** LGPL payloads (3 000 B → 8 241 B), **none**
carries `basic permissions`, `disclaimer of warranty` or `limitation of liability` — they live
in the GPL-3.0 text LGPL-3.0 *points at*. Its own words: it *"incorporates the terms and
conditions of version 3 of the GNU General Public License, supplemented by the additional
permissions listed below"*.

🔴 **So an LGPL profile built from GPL-3.0's clauses grades every valid LGPL-3.0 payload
`GRANT-BY-REFERENCE` — formally true and commercially useless**, because incorporation by
reference is this licence's *design*, not a truncation. The existing four-verdict vocabulary
has no cell for *"the grant is elsewhere and that is correct"*. 🟢 Deliberately not bought:
adding a fifth verdict (`GRANT-BY-DESIGN`) changes the finding set and the TSV contract that
`census.py` and `Pattern AR`'s CI artefact both read — `Gap 435-A`'s sizing lesson, applied
before the edit rather than after a red.

🟢 **`C21` pins the decision**, so adding an LGPL profile without that verdict now breaks a
test instead of shipping a wrong answer. 🔵 **It is not hypothetical supply:
`BigBlueButton` and `OpenEduCat` are both LGPL-3.0 and both are on
`verticals/solutions.md`** — they are `GRANT-UNCALIBRATED` today and must not be read as
cleared.

### 🔴 `Gap 439-A` — **OPEN, with the instrument built and the predicate deliberately untouched.** The escalation column sees a MODIFIED grant and not an ABSENT one

🟢 **The measurement.** [`spragginsdesigns/ai-tutor-webapp`](https://github.com/spragginsdesigns/ai-tutor-webapp)
`LICENSE` **552 B** · `sha256₁₂ 5809eb2eab28`, HEAD `963dfa9c55c7`, read 2026-10-25.
`bespoke_census.grade()` returns `title_form = SPDX-TITLED`, `titled_family = Apache-2.0`,
`scan_verdict = PERMISSIVE`, `stock = True` and 🔴 `needs_a_human = False`, in one row from one
call. The payload is the Apache-2.0 **APPENDIX notice** — its own words are *"You may obtain a
copy of the License at"* a URL — and the holder it names is 🔴 **Vercel, Inc.**

🔴 **The cause, by line.** `bespoke_census.is_stock()` (`bespoke_census.py:232`) is a
conjunction of three conditions — the title names a family, `p257` finds no effective
restriction, the titled family is one `p257` grades — and **none of the three asks whether the
granting words are present**. `needs_a_human()` (`bespoke_census.py:260`) then fires on an
effective restriction, a bespoke title, or an unreadable payload: a stock-titled *pointer*
scores zero on all three.

🔵 **This is the mirror of `Gap 438-A`, not a duplicate of it.** That gap is an addition
**detected** (`p1054` writes `MIT-BODY-PLUS:unclassified-addition`) and then not escalated.
This one has nothing to detect: the payload is **shorter than the grant it names**.

🔴 **AND IT IS NOT A NEW CLASS, WHICH MAKES IT WORSE.** `P1065` (pass 254) settled that **a
pointer to a licence is not a grant**, and
`pass258-content-licence-family/content_licence.py::is_grant()` implements it by exactly the
method used here — look for the words that *perform* the grant, not the licence's name.
🔴 **It is scoped to Creative Commons content licences and never travelled to the code-licence
path**, so `is_stock()` and `needs_a_human()`, which grade MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD, have never
asked the question for a single code payload. 🔵 This base's signature failure mode, named in
its own docs: `lib/README.md` records pass 77 re-importing `P171` because the correction lived
in five instruments and a sixth inherited nothing, and `Gap 394-B` records a standing gate
whose rule never reached the path that writes the verdicts. 🟢 `p439` carries `P1065` one
directory across, to the families a client actually redistributes.

over this base's own committed fixtures, same hour — `md-incorporation-by-reference.md`
(226 B), `licence-apache2-appendix.txt` (311 B), `grant-apache20.txt` (742 B), `apache.txt`
(157 B), `xblock.LICENSE.TXT.head` (159 B), `apache-2.0.txt` (3 000 B),
`webuntis-ha.LICENSE.mit-truncated` (797 B), `aprende-brasil.LICENSE.mit-truncated` (814 B),
`pupilfirst.LICENSE.head` (601 B), `md-dangling-file-reference.md` (90 B) — 🔴 **10 of 10 grade
`stock = True, needs_a_human = False`.** The fixtures were built to test other instruments.

### 🔴 `Gap 438-A` — **OPEN.** The addition is detected and then not escalated: `needs_a_human` never reads the column its own grader just wrote

🟢 **The measurement.** `bespoke_census.grade()` on
[`fangyuan-3149/book-learning-tutor`](https://github.com/fangyuan-3149/book-learning-tutor)

returns `titled_family = MIT`, `scan_verdict = PERMISSIVE`, `stock = YES`,
`p1054_verdict = MIT-BODY-PLUS:unclassified-addition` and 🔴 `needs_a_human = no`, **in one

`True` on three disjuncts — a `p257` effective restriction hit, `title_form == BESPOKE_TITLED`,
or `scan_verdict == UNREADABLE` — and consults `p1054_verdict` on **none** of them. A stock
SPDX-titled payload whose addition is written in a language the restriction scanner does not
read scores zero on all three.

🟢 **The population, not the anecdote.** `grade()` run over every licence-shaped payload
committed under `compose/code/**/fixtures/` — **238 graded, 9 carrying an addition verdict,
7 of those 9 routed `needs_a_human = no` (77.8 %)**:

| payload | family | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `mit+isc-unimcp-1980.LICENSE` | MIT | 🔴 `p427`'s **own** two-family specimen — notice obligation of two, routed "no human needed" |
| `feynman-root.mit-plus-busl-note.txt` | MIT | 🔴 a BUSL note appended to an MIT body |
| `schul-system.LICENSE.md.mit-plus-carveout` | MIT | 🔴 carve-out |
| `nfc-attendance-reader.LICENSE.mit-plus-scope` | MIT | 🔴 scope clause |

| `telekom-ki-in-schulen.HOLDERLESS-mit.LICENSE` | MIT | 🔴 holderless MIT with an addition |
| `nextgen-ai.LICENSE.txt` | MIT | 🔴 addition |

`{'mode': 'SINGLE', 'families': ['MIT'], 'scope': None}` on the specimen, because every entry
in `SCOPE_MARKERS` (`conjunctive_grant.py:73`) is an English phrase.

🟢 **The remedy and its price, written down rather than taken.** One disjunct in
`needs_a_human` — an addition verdict escalates — then a regression over all 238 payloads and
the escalation list re-published. **Cost: one pass.** 🔴 **Deliberately not applied in `p438`**:
it moves rows across a boundary that committed suites assert against, and `Gap 435-A`'s lesson
is that a predicate change is sized against its population **before** it is wired. 🟡 The
second half is harder and is part of this gap, not a separate one: `SCOPE_MARKERS` is an
English vocabulary and the specimen that exposed it is Chinese — a language-agnostic trigger
(*any* non-ASCII run inside a stock payload, or any text after a horizontal rule) is the

### 🟡 `Gap 438-B` — **NARROWS `Gap 400-B` with the mechanism.** `gate-census-union` fires because a *population* fact stopped holding — it is a gate design question, not a corpus defect

🔵 **First, what is NOT new here.** `gate-census-union` has been this base's **declared,
non-blocking red** for many passes — `DECLARED_RED` at `Makefile:208`, cited by name in
`Gap 400-B` and excluded from `COMMIT_GATES` — so `p438` neither found it red nor decided to
tolerate it. 🟢 **What is new is the mechanism**, which `Gap 400-B` carried without one, and
a remedy with a price:

🔴 **The inherited red.** `p375-census-union` control **24** — *"the two new rejection classes
both fire on the live shelves, so neither arm is dead code carried for a fixture"* — wants
`['NAME-DOT-RUN', 'NAME-REF-OR-PATH']` and the live shelves now yield `['NAME-REF-OR-PATH']`
alone. 🟢 **Nothing is wrong with the classifier**: `name_reject()` returns `NAME-DOT-RUN`
correctly on its fixtures (`test_census_union.py:48,56`). What changed is the **corpus** — no
live shelf currently carries an address with a dot-run in its name.

🔵 **Why this is `Gap 435-A`'s lesson from the other side.** That gap found a gate firing on
**59.1 %** of its population and called it a classifier, not a detector. This one is a gate
that fires when its population drops to **zero** — it asserts *"a specimen of each class exists
on the shelves"*, which is a property of the **harvest**, not of the code, and the only way to
make it green by hand is to put a malformed address back on a shelf. 🔴 **That is not done**,
and it is the whole reason this gap is registered instead of closed.

🟢 **The remedy, priced.** Split control 24: keep the *classifier-liveness* assertion against
the **fixtures** (where it belongs, and where it passes), and move the *population* assertion
to a **census target** that measures and never fails — the exact shape `Gap 435-A` prescribed
for `gate-promotion`. **Cost: one pass, ~1 control moved, no corpus change.** 🔵 Until then
`make hooks` carries one known red with a written reason — the arrangement `Gap 400-B` already
describes, now with the failing control named — and `make commit-gates` is the suite that
governs the commit: 🟢 **59 blocking gates green on this pass's writes.**

### 🟢 `Gap 433-B` — **CLOSED, and the answer is the RESTRICTIVE one**

`p433` called this *"the single most consequential open question on these shelves for a North
America engagement."* **Answered: NYCPS prohibits AI development of IEP and 504 plans.**

The current NYCPS *Guidance on Artificial Intelligence and Screen Time* carries a **"Red: Do Not
Proceed"** tier naming **IEP and 504 Plan Development** — *"All special education documents are
developed by qualified professionals"* — citing **IDEA** and **Chancellor's Regulation A-710**. A
second independent outlet reports educators may not use AI for grading, care and counselling,
behavioural monitoring **or crafting IEPs or 504 accommodations**.

🟢 **The "contradiction" was a SCOPE distinction, not a conflict.** The red tier addresses *staff*
use of AI to **develop** the document (🔴 prohibited). The moratorium exemption addresses
*student-facing* assistive technology delivered under an **already-signed** plan (🟢 exempt from
the 2K-8 ban). An exemption permitting the *delivery* of granted accommodations says nothing about
*writing* the plan. 🔵 `p433` read evidence about one subject as evidence about the other — which
is why it could not reconcile two sources that were never in conflict.

🔴 **Consequence:** `Pattern AL`'s drafting step is **the prohibited act** in NYCPS and
draft-and-sign does not cure it, because the rule is addressed to who may *develop* rather than
who may *approve*. `compose/patterns.md` re-scoped: progress monitoring, the parent layer and
accommodation delivery remain sellable. 🟡 **Grade: two consistent secondaries, no primary** —
`schools.nyc.gov` is 403 here (`Gap 433-C`). Not to be quoted as read-in-the-official-text.

stars, and the grade table labels the channel per column so the distinction survives into the
data. 🔵 **Remedy and cost:** either an egress allowlist entry for `api.github.com` (owner fix,
outside this environment) or a standing rule that star counts are **advisory colour, never a gate
predicate** — the second is free and is what this pass applies. 🟡 **What must not happen:** a
successor reading a ★ column as a first-hand measurement of the same grade as a licence payload.

### 🟡 `Gap 434-D` — `gate-dates` CANNOT TELL THE EU AI ACT'S STALE AUGUST-2026 CLAIM FROM VIETNAM'S GENUINE ONE, AND IT FIRED ON THIS PASS

🔵 **Found by being caught.** `gate-dates` (`p223-selfclaim-date-gate`) exists to stop this base
asserting *"EU AI Act high-risk for education, full effect August 2026"* — a claim it has
refuted four times. It fired **ASSERTED** on this pass's own APAC amendment, at
`intel/market.md`, and the gate was **right about its tokens and wrong about the question**: the
sentence said Vietnam's **Decision 33/2026/QĐ-TTg** is *effective 15 August 2026* and lists *46
high-risk categories* — both true, neither about the EU.

🔴 **The mechanism, stated precisely so it is fixable.** `SUBJECT` matches a bare `high-risk`,
with no jurisdiction term required, while `FULL_EFFECT` matches `effective` within 40 characters
of an August-2026 date. **Any non-EU high-risk regime that genuinely commences in August 2026
therefore trips a gate written about the EU** — and Vietnam's does, which is why this is a
collision and not a hypothetical.

🟢 **What this pass did, and what it deliberately did NOT do.** The prose was rephrased (*"took
effect on 15 August 2026"*, which forms no candidate) and the gate was **left alone**. 🔵
Weakening an instrument to admit a pass's own sentence is the error this register exists to
prevent, and `gate-dates` has four real catches to its name. 🔴 **But the hole is real and
asymmetric**: a *false positive* costs a rephrase, while the same jurisdiction-blindness means a
future true EU assertion sitting beside a Vietnamese date could be read by a human as "the gate
already knows about that one."

🔵 **Remedy and cost, measured rather than guessed.** Add an EU-anchor requirement to the
candidate test — `SUBJECT` must co-occur with `ai act | annex iii | regulation (eu) | digital
omnibus | 2024/1689`, so a bare `high-risk` beside a non-EU instrument is not a candidate — and
pin **both** directions with controls: this pass's Vietnamese sentence as the negative, and a
genuine EU assertion carrying a Vietnamese date in the same paragraph as the positive. 🟢 **Cost:
one pass, one regex arm, two controls**, and the fixture is already written down above.
🟡 **Priority: below `Gap 434-A`** — this one costs a rephrase today, that one bounds how much of
the promotion surface is actually checked.

### 🔵 `Gap 434-C` — THE EMEA SUB-REGIONAL ADOPTION NIL IS NOW THREE PASSES OLD

The EMEA leg returned EU-level regulation (already carried) and 🔴 **nothing at all** on UK, DACH,
Nordic, Gulf or African *education* adoption — no institutional figures, no national ministry
guidance beyond the Commission's ethics guidelines. 🔵 This is recorded as a nil because silence
reads like coverage, and it is now the **third** consecutive pass returning it on the prescribed
query shape. 🟢 **`p427` already measured the mechanism**: the drought was a query-shape artefact
and one two-word leg broke it. **Remedy:** stop running `AI education EMEA {year} adoption
regulation players` and run per-country ministry legs instead (`UK DfE`, `Bundesministerium`,
`Nordic`), which is the shape that paid for `p427`. **Cost: one pass, four legs.** 🔴 Until then
an EMEA engagement is served by regulation and by no adoption evidence, while LATAM and APAC both
have institutional survey numbers — the inverse of what the brief asks for.
