## 🆕 `p433`

### 🔴 `Gap 433-A` — THE TRENDING SHELVES ARE WRITE-ONLY: NOTHING PROMOTES A ROW, AND NOTHING AGES ONE OUT

`p433` found **five** high-traction addresses sitting in `agents/trending.md` and
`repos/trending.md` from earlier passes that had **never been promoted** to a curated shelf —
including [`dmoshehun-prog/learn-from-materials`](https://github.com/dmoshehun-prog/learn-from-materials)
at **1 118 ★ / 104 forks**, the highest-traction new education address this base has ever recorded.
Three were permissive on a first-hand payload read and are now rows in `agents/top.md`.

🔴 **The defect is structural, not clerical.** The trending files are append-only by contract —
correctly, because that is what makes them a trend record. But append-only with **no promotion
path** means traction accumulates unread: a row enters at 20 ★, grows to 1 118 ★, and no
instrument on this base ever looks at it again. `gate-shelf-consistency` checks that shelves do not
*disagree*; nothing checks that a curated shelf is not *missing* what the trending shelf already
holds.

**What would close it:** a gate that takes every address in the trending shelves, reads its current
star count, and fails when an address above a threshold (say 150 ★) carries a permissive grade and
appears in **no** curated shelf. That is a one-query-per-address online check, so it belongs
outside `hooks` like the other online arms. 🔵 **This pass did not build it** and says so rather
than implying it: the promotion was done by hand, which is exactly how `ACTION QO` stayed open for
eleven passes.

### 🟡 `Gap 433-B` — WHETHER NYC PROHIBITS AI-ASSISTED **IEP PLAN DEVELOPMENT** IS UNRESOLVED, AND IT GOVERNS `Pattern AL`

The NYC 2K-8 student-facing moratorium is 🟢 **confirmed and enacted** at `p433` (2026-09-02,
2026-27 school year) — that part closes a gap carried from `p386`. What does **not** close:

- The **March 2026 preliminary** guidance's red tier was reported to prohibit AI for grading,
  discipline, counselling and crisis intervention, academic placement, **and the development of
  special-education and 504 plans**.
- The **enacted** 2026-27 policy is quoted saying the moratorium *"does not apply to assistive
  technology and associated screen time, provided through a student's Individualized Education
  Program (IEP) or 504 Plan"* — an **exemption**, pointing the other way.
- A targeted search could **not** establish whether the plan-development prohibition survived into
  the enacted policy. One secondary says AI may not be used for "grading, behavior monitoring, or
  any decision involving student placement, promotion, or graduation" — and does not mention plan
  drafting either way.

🔴 **This is the single most consequential open question on these shelves for a North America
engagement**, because `Pattern AL` is an **IEP drafting assistant** and NYC is the largest school
district in the United States. 🔵 It is a gap and not a finding: nothing read this pass says
`Pattern AL` is unlawful in NYC, and nothing says it is permitted. `Pattern AL` now carries the
jurisdiction check in `compose/patterns.md`.

**What would close it:** the full text of the NYCPS *Guidance on Artificial Intelligence and Screen
Time* for 2026-27. Note the address has **moved** — reporting now cites
`schools.nyc.gov/about-us/policies/guidance-on-artificial-intelligence`, not the
`/vision-and-mission/artificial-intelligence/` path earlier passes would have tried.

### 🔴 `Gap 433-C` — THE EGRESS IS A FORGE-AND-REGISTRY ALLOWLIST, SO **NO GOVERNMENT OR NEWS PRIMARY CAN BE READ FROM HERE** (`Gap 430-C` generalised)

`Gap 430-C` recorded that the prescribed `curl -sI` cannot run here. `p433` measures the actual
shape, which is broader and worth stating precisely: **arbitrary hosts are refused at `CONNECT`
with a 403 by the network policy**, confirmed in the proxy's own failure log for
`www.schools.nyc.gov:443` and `www.beta.nyc:443`. `github.com` and the package registries work —
which is why every licence verdict on these shelves is genuinely first-hand — but **a statute, a
ministry circular, a district policy or a news report cannot be read at source from inside a
scheduled run**.

🔵 **The consequence, stated so no reader mistakes the grade:** every regulatory claim on these
shelves is **secondary-sourced by construction**. This base's 🟢/🟡/🔴 grades on regulatory items
mean *"corroborated across independent secondaries"*, never *"read in the official text"*. That is
a real ceiling on `intel/market.md` and it cannot be lifted from inside a run. **What would close
it:** an egress allowlist entry for `*.gov`, `*.europa.eu` and the major education outlets, or an
owner-run leg that fetches the primaries and commits them to `evidence/`.

### 🔴 `Gap 433-D` — THE ROTATION STILL HAS NOT ROTATED (`Gap 432-A`, `Gap 430-A`, FOURTH CONSECUTIVE PASS)

The mechanism is unchanged and is now re-confirmed a fourth time: a scheduled run is required to
develop on its own `claude/*` branch, so the `rotation.json` advance it pushes lands on **that
branch**, which is never merged to `main`; the next run clones `main` and reads `next: 8` again.
This pass advanced `rotation.json` to `{"next": 9, "last_industry": "education"}` and pushed it to
its assigned branch — **reproducing the failure once more, by design, because the run is not
permitted to push to `main`.**

🔴 **Unfixable from inside a scheduled run**, and the fix is an owner action. It needs one of:
(a) a merge of a rotation branch to `main`; (b) rotation state in a store a run may write durably;
(c) a scheduler that passes the industry in as a parameter instead of reading it from a repository
the runs cannot update. 🔵 Option (c) is the only one that cannot silently regress.

## 🆕 `p430`

### 🔴 `Gap 430-A` — THE ROTATION HAS NOT ROTATED SINCE 2026-08-02, AND THIS REPOSITORY IS THE SYMPTOM

**Severity: higher than any licence finding on these shelves**, because it governs whether
the other eleven industries are researched at all.

`rotation.json` in `gmilano/globant-kb` has read `next: 8` (education) since
**2026-08-02**, with `last_industry: technology`. This repository has taken **429 passes**
at ~23–26 per day in that window. `gaming`, `legal`, `financial`, `healthcare`, `media`,
`retail`, `travel`, `technology`, `automotive`, `energy` and `enterprise` have had **zero**.

**Mechanism, established by inspection of `globant-kb` this pass:**
1. Each scheduled run is required to develop on its own `claude/*` branch and is forbidden
   from pushing to `main`.
2. The run advances `rotation.json` and pushes it — to that throwaway branch.
3. The branch is never merged. `gmilano/globant-kb` currently carries **1 928** such
   branches.
4. The next run clones `main`, reads `next: 8`, and does education again.

The rotation write has therefore succeeded on every run and taken effect on none.

🔴 **This cannot be fixed from inside a scheduled run** — the fix is precisely the action
the runs are forbidden to take. It needs one of: a merge of a rotation branch to `main`;
a scheduled prompt that derives the industry from the date (e.g. `floor(hours since epoch)
mod 12`) so no shared write is needed; or rotation state held somewhere a run may write.

### 🟡 `Gap 430-B` — a permissive grade has no re-read date anywhere on these shelves

`Trend 9` names the mechanism: three passes read `pengusto/google-classroom-mcp` as MIT,
all three correctly, and the grant changed underneath them on 2026-10-23. The shelves
record a family and a SHA but no *as-of* date that an engagement can age out. Until a row
carries one, "MIT" on this base means "MIT when somebody last looked", and nothing says
when that was.

### 🔵 `Gap 430-C` — `curl -sI` is prescribed and cannot run here

The task prescribes `curl -sI` for URL verification. Every `github.com` request from this
host returns **403** from the egress proxy. A successor that follows the instruction
literally and believes the output will mark the entire corpus dead. Working channels are
recorded in `agents/trending.md` under `p430`.

### 🔵 `Gap 426-C` — CONTINUES (fourth consecutive pass)

The prescribed leg `top open source AI agents education {year} github MIT` returned **zero**
education-specific MIT agents again. `p427` named the mechanism and this pass confirms it:
the supply is built as **MCP servers named after the platform** (Canvas, Moodle, Classroom,
Blackboard), so a leg keyed on the word "education" cannot see it. The leg should be
retired or re-keyed rather than run a fifth time.

## Pass 391 · 2026-10-22 — **THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE ERROR, AND THIS TIME IT COST A RECOMMENDATION PUBLISHED THE SAME DAY: A STALE UPSTREAM IS NOT A DEAD DEPENDENCY. 🔴 THE REAL GAP IS THAT THIS BASE'S HARVEST HISTORY HAS NO PROMOTION MECHANISM TO ITS SHELVES.**

  constraint rather than a shelf note.** [`dmitry-viskov/pylti1.3`](https://github.com/dmitry-viskov/pylti1.3)
  (MIT) last moved **2022-11-21 — 1,431 days**; PyPI `PyLTI1p3` **2.0.0, published 2022-11-20**, 29
  releases, none since. Node ([`Cvmcosta/ltijs`](https://github.com/Cvmcosta/ltijs), npm v7.0.7,
  2026-10-06) and PHP ([`packbackbooks/lti-1-3-php-library`](https://github.com/packbackbooks/lti-1-3-php-library),
  packagist v6.4.4, 2026-09-23) are both live. Almost every agent on these shelves is Python, so the
  interop edge must be a **separate Node or PHP service in front of the agent** — a deployment
  component every LMS-integration proposal has to cost. 🔵 **Closing this gap means a maintained
  Python implementation existing, not a workaround**; until then the workaround is the recommendation.

- **`Gap 391-B`: the district-targeting instrument is North America only, and there is no analogue
  for any other region.** [`pipeworx-io/mcp-education-data`](https://github.com/pipeworx-io/mcp-education-data)
  (MIT) makes a US pilot pricable before the first call — per-district enrolment, **per-pupil spend**
  and **Census child-poverty counts** (the Title I basis). **Nothing equivalent exists here for EMEA,
  APAC or LATAM.** Brazil's INEP and Mexico's SEP publish education statistics; nothing was found this
  pass exposing them as a queryable granted component, and `zenodo.org` / `doi.org` — the likeliest
  carriers of a research-deposited one — are **both DNS-unreachable**. 🔵 Recorded as a
  **channel-and-supply** gap, not as a claim the data does not exist. Stated explicitly on
  `intel/market.md` under LATAM because silence there would read as coverage.

- **`Gap 391-C`: there is no granted proctoring row, and proctoring is an Annex III high-risk
  surface.** [`InCruiter-NewProducts/proctoring-sdk`](https://github.com/InCruiter-NewProducts/proctoring-sdk)
  is published on npm (2026-09-25) and its repository is **unreadable** — the `p388`
  *published-but-unreadable* class. Proctoring, AI-detection in assessment and exam scoring are
  exactly the surfaces the EU AI Act names, so a studio asked about them has **nothing permissive to
  start from** on these shelves. 🔵 A blobless clone cannot tell private from deleted, so this is
  `DEAD-OR-PRIVATE`, not "removed".

  does it except a pass that happens to look.** This is now the **third instance of one error**, and

  |---|---|---|

### 🔴 `Gap 386-C` CLOSED, and it was the same error `p386` itself diagnosed

`Gap 386-C` called LATAM-native agent supply *"structural, not a search artefact"* after a fourth
consecutive null leg. **It was a search artefact.** Two legs phrased in Portuguese and Spanish
returned six candidates, **three granted** —
[LabSirius/TutorIA](https://github.com/LabSirius/TutorIA) (MIT, Colombia, Open edX XBlock),
[GuilhermeScarpini/agente-bncc-professores](https://github.com/GuilhermeScarpini/agente-bncc-professores)
(MIT, Brazil, BNCC-code-gated generation),
[thiagoudweb/techTutor](https://github.com/thiagoudweb/techTutor) (MIT, Brazil, UFAPE) — all read
first-hand today and now shelved as **Tier 4** on [`agents/top.md`](../agents/top.md).
🔴 **Root cause, and it is this base's own `Pattern L` step 12 one level up:** `p386` established
that *a count of addresses is not a count of grants*. The twin error is **a null leg reported as a
null supply**. Worse, three of these addresses were already in `agents/trending.md`'s harvest
history and had never reached a shelf — so the shelves claimed an absence the base did not have.
🟢 **The replacement claim, which is defensible:** what LATAM lacks is not agents but **tenancy,
support and institution-grade packaging** — recorded on `intel/market.md` as LATAM opportunity 7.

   bug; the contract is documented as STOP/GO at the make layer with the three-way in stdout
   and in the script's own exit code.

   *"opposite"* — so it confirmed while under-reporting its own result.

### 🔴 The finding, in one sentence

🔵 `p349`'s alias gate exists to catch one hazard, and its own docstring names the
mechanism: *"GitHub keeps every former address of a transferred or renamed repository
answering FOREVER, by redirect."* 🟢 **A redirect serves ONE repository**, so the old
address must answer with the **same ref set**. 🔴 **Five register rows do not, and the
gate has been enforcing them onto correct shelves:**

| group | the address the register called `STALE` | its refs | the canonical side's refs | shared `HEAD` | `p370` |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `moodler-mcp` | `dymayo/moodler-mcp` | **2** | **62** | `4e6139eb9c6b` | 🔴 **fork** → `DISTINCT` |
| `mcp-brasil` | `dasgltd/mcp-brasil` | **50** | **99** | `2efb258370b1` | 🔴 **fork** → `DISTINCT` |
| `purdue-mcp` | `rohanmuppa/purdue-mcp` | **2** | **4** | `6922f1f301dd` | 🔴 **fork** → `DISTINCT` |
| `lxhive` | `leogaggl/lxhive` | **3** | **187** | `cffee6d90ca9` | 🔴 **fork** → `DISTINCT` |
| `openpronounce` | `chinobv/openpronounce` | **3** | **9** | `74bc17ea406e` | 🔴 **fork** → `DISTINCT` |

🟢 **The `purdue-mcp` pair is the proof that needs no interpretation.**
`sharziki/purdue-mcp` carries `refs/pull/1/head` at `85f66af9019d`, and that sha **is**
`rohanmuppa/purdue-mcp`'s `refs/heads/fix/current-term-default`. One repository opened a
pull request against the other. 🔴 Two repositories in a contributor relationship cannot
be one address and its redirect, and the register said they were.

🔵 **Why `refs/pull/*` is kept in the fingerprint rather than filtered as noise:** pull
refs accrue to the repository that *receives* pull requests, so a fork starts with none.
It is the strongest fork discriminator GitHub exposes over the git protocol.

🟢 **17 of 22 `STALE` rows survive**, among them `stanfordnlp/edu-convokit` ≡
`EduNLP/edu-convokit`, whose ref sets are byte-identical. The instrument is not a
licence to disbelieve the register; it is the test the register's own header asked for.

### 🔴 The shelf correction: `p367` fixed a gate by editing the shelf the wrong way

| | |
|---|---|
| `p367` published | *"`agents/top.md` carried `INGInious/INGInious` as a live row address — the pre-rename half of a pair `p366` had itself just identified. 🟢 Fixed (the row cites `UCL-INGI/INGInious`)"* |
| 🔴 `p370` measured | Fetching `github.com/UCL-INGI/INGInious` **lands on `INGInious/INGInious`** — breadcrumb `INGInious / INGInious`, **243 ★**, no rename notice. The same fetch of `github.com/INGInious/INGInious` stays put. |
| 🔴 So | **`UCL-INGI/INGInious` is the STALE address.** `p367` rewrote **two correct live rows** into it, in `agents/top.md` and `repos/foundations.md`. |
| 🔴 And why nobody noticed | `ALIAS_REGISTER` pointed at **`p349`'s** register, which carries **no `INGInious` row at all**. `p350` built a register with the row in it — 21 `CANONICAL`, 22 `STALE` against `p349`'s 6 and 7 — and **nothing was ever pointed at it.** The gate went green on a question it was not being asked. |
| 🟢 `p370` | Both rows restored to `INGInious/INGInious`; the pair table now carries the direction and marks the stale side; `ALIAS_REGISTER` now points at `p370`'s register, which is `p350`'s superset with the five demotions applied. |

🔵 **The lesson is not about INGInious, and it is not `p367`'s carelessness.** A gate is
only as current as the data file it is handed. `p350` improved the register and left the
`?=` default alone, so for twenty passes the strictest identity gate on this base read a
register two passes behind the best one available — and the one pass that acted on a red
finding from it had no row to check itself against.

### 🟢 `ACTION ZZ-cb` / `Gap 475` closed — the slug is not the domain, and now something checks

`p367` declared this gap, priced it as the cheapest on the base, and measured a **40 %**
trap rate on five permissive rows. 🟢 **`p370` built the check and ran it on 63 addresses
drawn from `Gap 473`'s net-new class, every verdict read from the README payload with the
root tree as the fallback channel.**

| | first draft | after the four fixes |
|---|---:|---:|
| `EDUCATION` | 36 | 🟢 **50** |
| `SLUG-TRAP` | 15 | 6 |
| `NOT-EDUCATION` | 7 | 6 |
| `WEAK` | 3 | 1 |
| `NO-README` / `NO-EVIDENCE` | 2 | 0 |
| **precision** (hand-adjudicated) | 36/36 = **100 %** | 50/50 = **100 %** |
| **recall** | 36/54 = **66.7 %** | 🟢 **50/54 = 92.6 %** |

🔴 **The four traps that are real, and the two sharpest are new:**
[`pawelkn/xapi-rs`](https://github.com/pawelkn/xapi-rs) (MIT) and
[`peterszombati/xapi-node`](https://github.com/peterszombati/xapi-node) (BSD-3-Clause)
are clients for **xStation5, a forex broker's trading API** — in education `xAPI` is the
Experience API, and the name match has nothing behind it.
[`cern-qti/quask`](https://github.com/cern-qti/quask) (Apache-2.0) is CERN's **Quantum
Technology Initiative**, not IMS QTI.
[`totoketchup/adaptive-multispeaker-separation`](https://github.com/totoketchup/adaptive-multispeaker-separation)
(MIT) is speech separation, not adaptive learning.

🔴 **And the four defects in `p370`'s own first draft, each named by the string that caused it:**

| | the defect | the specimen |
|---|---|---|
| `D1` | one **STRONG** anchor was not treated as sufficient — two anchors of any kind were demanded | [`bycs-lp/moodle-ci-workflows`](https://github.com/bycs-lp/moodle-ci-workflows), *"reusable workflows for the Moodle plugins of bycs-lp"*, called a trap on the word `moodle` |
| `D2` | a word boundary hides a strong token inside a **compound name** | [`surlabs/aichatformoodle`](https://github.com/surlabs/aichatformoodle), whose entire README is the line `# AIChatForMoodle` |
| `D3` | no morphology — and English consonant doubling is still not derived, it is carried | [`quizlar/mcp-server`](https://github.com/quizlar/mcp-server): `quiz` missed `quizzes`, `grade` missed `graded` |
| `D4` | the lexicon was English-plus-Iberian, so a **national instrument** reads as out-of-domain | [`3121n/nor-data-udir-mcp`](https://github.com/3121n/nor-data-udir-mcp), which wraps the Norwegian Directorate for Education's national school and kindergarten registers, in Norwegian (`skoler`, `barnehager`) |

🔵 **`D4` is `Gap 476`/`ACTION ZZ-cc` arriving from the other direction.** The same
monolingual assumption that makes the prescribed EMEA and APAC region legs return
analyst prose also made the domain filter blind to the national instruments those legs
exist to find. One lexicon fixes both halves.

🟡 **Honesty about the recall figure, stated because it is otherwise misleading:** all
four defects were derived from **this pass's 63-slug sample**, so **92.6 % is in-sample**.
It is published as such and registered as `Gap 480`.

### 🟡 What running the suite cost this pass, published because `p366` and `p367` both made the opposite choice

🟢 **`make hooks` was run three times: once at `p369`'s HEAD (33/34, `gate-alias-canonical`
RED), once after this pass's content was written (32/36), and once after the repairs
(36/36).** The middle run is the interesting one, and every finding in it was a defect in
**this pass's own work**, not in the shelves:

| Gate | What it caught in `p370`'s work | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `gate-offline` → `p253-captured-body-census` | this pass's new `probe_tree.sh` was an **unpinned** shell site — *"a live site missing from the pins is caught"* | pin regenerated with the instrument's own `write_pins`, never hand-written: `BODY-ONLY 1 0 0 0` |
| `gate-offline` → `p253-gate-propagation` | 🔴 **both new gate recipes could print `PASS` while a step failed** — the exact shape `p253` built that control to stop | `\|\| exit 1` added to both |
| `recount` | 🔴 **this pass's own prose deleted two of the five registered claim anchors** and left a third stale (`11` published against `52` measured) | all three sentences restated in the anchored form, derived by `make recount` |
| `gate-ladder-case` | the ratchet rose **17 → 18**: `domain_check.py` used the bare token `readme` as a **channel label** and a test used it in a label string, and the path census cannot tell a label from a path | labels renamed to `readme-payload` / `tree-enumeration`; ratchet back to **17** |
| `gate-census-currency` | 🔴 the address triple went stale the moment this pass wrote to the shelves — **2 640 → 2 679** | re-derived **as the last act** and restated in the live section: **2 679 → 33 → 2 646** (1.23 %) |

🔵 **Three of the five are the same lesson from different directions: a pass's own prose
is shelf content, and the gates that read the shelves read it too.** Deleting a sentence
that a gate anchors on is a defect even when the replacement sentence is more accurate —
which is why the anchored forms are restored verbatim and the new numbers put inside them.

🔵 **A naming note, so nobody re-walks it.** `compose/code/` already contained a
`p370-gap-gate/` — dated **2026-10-05** and committed at **pass 115** — because the
instrument directories were once numbered on a counter of their own that ran past 370
(`p969-root-only-licence-reach`, `p1057-licence-path-case`). 🟢 Current practice is the
PASS number (`p367-bare-slug-channel`), which is what this pass's three directories use.
🟡 The collision is cosmetic and nothing imports across it, but a reader grepping
`p370-` will find a 2026-10-05 artefact among this pass's.

🟡 **And one scope note on `gate-ladder-case`, recorded rather than fixed.** The path
census reads a bare `readme` or `licence` token in code as a *path spelling*, so an
instrument that merely *labels a channel* scores as a single-spelling ladder. `p367` hit
this too and resolved it the same way. 🔵 Renaming costs nothing and keeps the ratchet
meaningful, so no change was made to `p283`'s grader — but a successor building an
instrument in this area should expect the collision and name its labels accordingly.

### 🔴 The findings that cost the most to learn

🔴 **1. A refusal is a fact about the host you asked.** `p297` concluded *"no raw path"* from 403s at
`github.com` and `api.github.com` — two **other** hosts — and `p299` then graded 14 of 15 rows
sidebar-only on that bound. 🔴 **Worse: the loop for the host nobody asked was already in this
repository.** [`compose/code/lib/probe_payload.sh`](../compose/code/lib/probe_payload.sh) — *"source
this, do not rewrite it"* — answered correctly on the **first call**, including both traps its own
header documents. 🔵 **A bound written in prose was believed over a tool sitting in the tree.** Full
entry: `T-p300a`.

🔴 **2. A fail-fast chain of independent checks sheds coverage silently.** `gate-identity`'s four
findings were one shape: **a sibling repository cited in a row's description cell, harvested as a
second recommendation.** The gate's own docstring had already named that error class at *file* scope
and fixed it there; it survived at *row* scope. 🟢 **Fixed asymmetrically** — `ADDRESS-TWICE` now
scopes to the row's **subject** (the first address-bearing cell; measured: **153 of 379** live
address rows carry none in cell 1, so a cell-1 rule would blind the gate on 40 % of the shelf), while
`ALIAS-PAIR-LIVE` **keeps whole-row scope**, because control C6 pins a live `p283` finding that a
symmetric fix would have deleted. **17 controls — 12 original plus 5 new — all pass.** 🟢 `hooks` now
runs **every** gate with a per-gate verdict: **15/15 green across 62 instrument suites**, against 55
when the chain stopped early.

🔴 **3. A layer backlog built by substring match on the slug is not a layer backlog.** Of
`ACTION PG-4`'s seven named slugs, **three were already on this base's tables** and one —
`xapi-labs/xapi-cli` — **is not the Experience API at all.** 🔵 `p299` published the rule that would
have caught three of the four *in the same breath as the instruction that made them*: it applied
*"match only table rows"* to the **shelf** side of the diff and never to the **candidate** side.

🔴 **4. A non-nil leg is not a productive leg.** Checked mechanically against the committed
`intel/market.md`: **21 datums examined, 17 already carried, 4 new** — and **the four mandated
regional legs produced ZERO between them** against 3 from one directed leg. This corrected two of
this pass's own draft claims, including a carried-check that was itself wrong on first run. Entry:
`T-p300d`.

**partitioned before it is prioritised**, or a pass will spend its budget on the cluster that is
easiest to enumerate.

### 🔴 And the standing gate was RED at `HEAD`, which no pass-273 artefact mentions

🟢 **`p274` ran `make hooks` — and it failed, on the committed tree, before this pass had changed
anything.** Proven rather than asserted: `git stash` → the identical **6 of 166** controls fail → `git
stash pop`.

```
6/166 FAILED
  - ordering on agents/top.md is AGREE or UNDECIDABLE (reference doc)
  - agents/top.md: if it carries dated sections they are ordered
  - ordering on repos/foundations.md …            (and the same pair)
  - ordering on verticals/solutions.md …          (and the same pair)
```

🔵 **The mechanism, and it is a slow-growing defect rather than a mistake.** `p261`'s invariant is that a
shelf carrying two or more pass-numbered `##` headings must carry them **non-increasing in file order** —
the shape a shelf has when each pass **prepends**. 🔴 **These three reference docs were built by passes
that APPENDED**, so their pass numbers ran `273, 269, 268, 270, 272` (`agents/top.md`), `270, 272`
(`repos/foundations.md`) and `270, 271, 272` (`verticals/solutions.md`). **Each append was individually
harmless; the second one in ascending order tripped the invariant, and it has been red since.**

🟢 **Fixed by permuting the pass sections into descending order within their existing positions** —
content untouched, non-pass sections untouched — and `make hooks` now exits **0** with **45 PASS**.
⚠️ **One consequence recorded because it bit this pass's own prose:** the permutation **moves line
numbers**, so a finding must cite a **row and a section**, never a line number. Three of this pass's own
sentences had to be rewritten for exactly that reason.

🔴 **The deeper point is why nobody noticed.** `p261`'s own section records that the gate *"ran for the
first time in ten passes"* and was red then too; `p251` and `p252` both recorded `make` as **not runnable
from their session**. 🔵 **A gate that is only run when someone remembers is a gate whose verdict is
unknown**, and the invariant it enforces is precisely the kind no reader notices. 🟢 **`make hooks` now
also runs `make recount`** (`T43`), so the two cheapest checks on this base share one entry point.

### 🔵 The lesson for the ledger

🔵 **Extending a ten-pass set.** `p251`: *unwired knowledge.* `p253`: *nothing consumes the wire.* `p254`: *the base inherits its own conclusions about what is impossible.* `p255`: *a claim adopted at a retraction inherits the retraction's credibility.* `p256`: *a gate's existence was read as its coverage.* `p257`: *a classifier's scope, not its vocabulary, was the hole.* `p258`: *a refusal from one endpoint was generalised to the whole channel.* `p259`: *a ladder keyed on the PATH could not see that one path carries two KINDS of evidence.* `p260`: *a ladder's REACH was read as its RUN.*

🟢 **`p261`: the gate that would have caught all of this was runnable the whole time, and three passes recorded one session's refusal as a property of the base — so the only standing check this KB has was red for a full pass and read as unknown.**

🔵 **And the pass's second lesson, which is the first one turned inward:** `p260` wrote `reservation_verdict()` to stop a false retraction and `p261` watched it cause one, because the guard was keyed on the payload and **a payload is not one grant**. 🟢 Every key in this sequence has been one level finer than the last — `path` *(`p258`)*, `(path, payload)` *(`p259`)*, `(path, row)` *(`p260`)*, and now **`(payload, section)` and `(ecosystem, grammar)`**. 🔴 The pattern worth watching is that each new guard, written at the newest key, is wrong at the next one down.

### 🔴 The box `ACTION XE` earned: **naming a family without closing the arm would have made the verdict WORSE**

🔴 **`P241`'s blanket-denial branch is gated on `[ "$__f" = "UNCLASSIFIED" ]`.** Emitting a family NAME therefore **removes** that protection — `$__f` stops being `UNCLASSIFIED` and the branch does not run. Combined with a default arm that permits, the "improvement" XE asked for would have turned a payload that at least passed through a denial branch into a **named** family that skips it and is permitted by default. 🔵 XE suspected the arm; it did not see that the two defects compose.

🟢 **AND THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS THE WRONG ONE, also by measurement.** Inverting the default to deny would have denied every OSI family this base emits and does not list. Measured instance: **`CC0-1.0` does not match the `CC-*` glob**, so it was reaching the default arm and returning `ALLOWED` *by accident* — the right answer by the wrong road. A blanket inversion would have broken it. Hence: closed enumeration, explicit allow arms, and a `family-arm closure` control that reads the arm patterns **out of the source** and fails if any emittable family could reach the net.

  that wrote it.** In ralph, `POST` enriches authority and then forwards; `PUT` forwards and
  then enriches *(the comments say so: "Enrich statement before forwarding" … "Finish
  enriching statements after forwarding")*, and `forwarding.py` sends `json=statements`
  verbatim. 🔴 **So a forwarded `PUT` carries the client's own unvalidated `authority` — or
  none — while the copy stored locally is correctly attributed.** A client with no
  `authority/write` scope cannot forge attribution locally and **can** forge it downstream.
  🔵 Not spec-driven and not a reading of prose: two call orders, eleven lines apart.

  trains on facial-affect labels *(boredom, confusion, engagement, frustration)*. **`AI Act`

  `package.json`. 🔵 **The best permissive schema on the shelf has the one defect that is hardest

  sentence. 🔵 **A file probe sees one licence where there are two, and the second one is the one
  that travels into a deliverable.**

  unverifiable from here.** `2026-08-02` → **`2027-12-02`**, amending regulation cited as
  **Regulation (EU) 2026/1744**, Article `50`(2) marking **`2026-12-02`**, Article `5` prohibitions
  unchanged. 🔴 Secondary sources only, and they disagree on whether it is in force;
  `eur-lex.europa.eu` is `ENOTFOUND` here. 🔵 **Plan to the earlier date.**

### 🆕 🔴 `ACTION JT` — `gap 118` was a question, not a hole

🟢 **Query strings recorded verbatim, per `T227`, in
[`evidence/mea-region-queries.2026-10-13-p173.tsv`](../evidence/mea-region-queries.2026-10-13-p173.tsv).
Channel: `WebSearch`, US-indexed, `2026-10-13`. Six formulations, `6` returned.**

| formulation | returned | countries placed |
|---|---|---|
| `AI education adoption Middle East 2026 regulation players` | 🟢 yes | UAE, Saudi Arabia |
| `AI education Africa 2026 adoption regulation edtech` | 🟢 yes | Kenya, Rwanda, South Africa, Nigeria |
| `edtech AI Gulf GCC UAE Saudi Arabia 2026 schools adoption` | 🟢 yes | UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain |
| `AI curriculum policy Nigeria Kenya South Africa 2026` | 🟢 yes | Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa |
| `artificial intelligence education strategy Egypt Morocco Israel 2026` | 🟡 partial | Egypt, Morocco — 🔴 **Israel returned NOTHING** |
| `African open source edtech AI startups 2026 funding github` | 🟡 partial | Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania — 🔴 **no African-origin open-source repo** |

🆕 🔴 **`T254` — p172's EMEA queries could not have returned Middle East or Africa, and the gap
recorded their silence as the region's.** A region abbreviation is not a search term. *"EMEA"*
indexes European coverage because European institutions publish in the languages and venues the
index is built from; the Middle East and Africa answer to **country names**. `gap 118` said *"the
largest unexamined bucket"* and the bucket was unexamined because of how it was asked for.
🟢 **Register rule: a region bucket is searched by naming its COUNTRIES, and a region that returns
nothing is only a finding once `≥4` of its countries have been named individually.**

🆕 🔴 **And the substantive finding, which is a market statement and not a methodology one:
the Middle East leads the world on MANDATE and Africa leads on GOVERNANCE DEBT, and they are the
same opportunity from opposite ends.** The UAE and Saudi Arabia have made AI education
**compulsory** in public schools from the `2025/26` year — the UAE from age four, KSA embedding AI
and coding across all school levels — while a WISE/Ashesi survey of `47` African higher-education
institutions (February `2026`) found **`6` in `10` have no formal AI governance framework at all**,
and that `64%` of African edtech startups build for K-12 while **under `2%`** build AI for higher
education. 🔴 **`gap 124` replaces `gap 118`: this KB has the policy surface for both and `0`
open-source repositories originating in either.**

🟢 **The two `LGPL` mismatches were verified against authoritative upstream metadata rather than
memory — mojohaus/Apache CXF for `aopalliance`, the Maven Central POM for `dnsjava` — and the JUnit
row against `repo1.maven.org/maven2/junit/junit/3.8.1/junit-3.8.1.pom`, which declares *"Common
Public License Version 1.0"* in its own `<licenses>` block.**
🟢 **The JUnit mismatch is by IDENTIFIER, barely by EFFECT: `CPL-1.0` is the IBM Public License
re-stewarded. Report it as an identifier error and do not inflate it.**

🆕 🟢 **`T230` — the MECHANISM of `gap 117` is generic-blob reuse.** Both `LGPL` mismatches have a
blob byte-identical to the manifest's own generic `LGPL2.1.license.txt`. A component file that is a
copy of a family file is evidence of a FAMILY and never of that component's grant. `8` of `86`
paths are in this class; `2` are wrong and `6` are right by coincidence.
🆕 🔴 **`T231` — p171 read `0` hostile because it tested the wrong WORD.** `ACTION JK` used
`commercial_use_ok()`, a NONCOMMERCIAL-phrase test. `jta.license.txt` grants *"internal use only …
for which the corresponding fee has been paid"* and forbids modification and decompilation, and
never says *"noncommercial"*. **A phrase test is silent on every proprietary licence that withholds
redistribution instead of commerce.** The `0` was true about the question asked and false about the
question meant.
🆕 🔴 **`T232` — `compose/code/lib/license_family.sh` cannot see `Apache-1.1`.** It answers `BSD`
for the Apache Software License 1.1, including for the file named `apache1.1.license.txt`. That is
`25` of `86` paths here. `Apache-1.1` is BSD-SHAPED but carries its own attribution clause
(*"This product includes software developed by the Apache Software Foundation"*), which is how p172
detects it. 🔴 **This is a defect in a SHARED hardened control, so every instrument that sources it
inherits the error.**
🆕 🔵 **`T224` RE-FIRED, on p172's own instrument.** p172's first hostility test searched bodies for
withholding language and returned `34` raw hits, `26` of them ordinary `Apache-2.0` and `LGPL` text
caught on phrases like *"shall not modify"*. The finding survived only by moving to the title
block — which is `P237`, written in this KB since pass 77. **Three consecutive passes have now
broken the same rule on first attempt. A rule that has to be remembered is not a control.**

### 🆕 🔴 `ACTION IZ` is the first action whose falsifier fired and then un-fired

🔴 **The falsifier was *"refuted if `≥1` of the `10` returns a synonym hit"*, and the `13`-term probe
returned exactly `1` across `11 684` tracked files.** 🟢 **Cited in full:
`plastic-labs/tutor-gpt` `pnpm-lock.yaml:1263`,
`integrity: sha512-grOjVNN8P3hjJn/eIETF1wwd12DdnwFDoyceUJLYYdkpbwq3nLi+4fqrTAONx7XDALqlL220wC/RHSC/QTI/0w==`
— `\bQTI\b` matching inside base64, because `/` is a word boundary.**
🟢 **Excluding `17` lockfiles across `8` of the `10` trees takes every one of the `13` terms to `0`
of `10`, and p167's published *"`10` of `15` trees have no interop standard"* SURVIVES on `13` terms
instead of `5`.**
🔵 **Why it is recorded loudly rather than quietly fixed: a pass that had published the raw number
would have overturned a CORRECT finding on the strength of a hash, and the register would have shown
a falsifier firing — the most trustworthy-looking outcome this shelf produces.**
🔴 **The fix is a FILE CLASS, not a pattern: `\bqti\b` case-insensitive returns the same single hit,
so no amount of regex tightening would have caught it.**

## 🔴 The control nobody registered this pass — and it cost `752 MB`

🔴 **This pass reached for `git clone --depth=1 --filter=blob:none` on Moodle expecting a
treeless discount, and measured `752 MB` on disk against p160's `746 MB` full shallow clone.**
🟢 **The filter is real; the CHECKOUT defeats it by re-fetching every blob in the working tree.**
🟢 **`--no-checkout`, or a sparse checkout of the directory under test, is the instrument that
actually saves.** 🔴 **And in this specific case neither was needed: the two files the pass
wanted — `public/lib/db/install.xml` and `public/ai/classes/privacy/provider.php` — are two
`raw` reads once the paths are known.**
🔵 **`P161-C` records it so the next pass does not re-buy the same `752 MB`.**

### 🔴 The instrument defect this pass produced, and the reason it is the pass's main finding

🔵 **Fifth consecutive pass whose first draft erred — and the first where the error was invisible
to the falsifier guarding it.**

`ACTION DM`'s repaired instrument, on its first run, reported `krzysztofbury/librus-mcp` as
**23 literal / 0 dynamic**. p141 had reported **0 literal / 23 dynamic**. 🔴 **Both readings are
drawn from the same 23 sites, and none of those sites is in the server the package ships** — 21
are in `legacy_reference/src/server.py`, 2 in `scripts/qualify_native.py`. The shipped surface is
**35** `server.tool(annotations=…)(fn)` calls in `src/librus_mcp/`.

🔴 **The tier share was identical under both readings.** A falsifier phrased as *"the statistic
must not move by more than five points"* passes any error that is symmetric across the
population — including measuring the wrong population.

🟢 **What caught it:** one subject's verdict flipped between two instruments, which prompted
opening the repository and counting by hand. 🔵 **Adopted as `T37`**, with three enforcements:
`NOT_SHIPPED` in `surface_gate2.py`, `test_not_shipped_trees_are_excluded`, and a
`not_shipped_delta` column so a whole-tree/shipped-tree disagreement is visible per row instead
of pooled into a share.

🔴 **And `ACTION DS` is registered against the fix itself**, because `NOT_SHIPPED` excludes
`scripts/` — which is where `global-education-mcp` keeps the very generator this pass praised.

### 🔴 The instrument defect this pass produced, and why its direction matters

🔴 **The matcher's first version missed the MIT grant it was built to find** — licence headers wrap
inside comment blocks (`free of\n * charge`) and a contiguous-phrase match returns nothing. Caught
by the test suite before any number was published; comment leaders and whitespace are now collapsed
first.

🔵 **Stated because the bug flattered the pass's own expectation.** It would have produced the same
headline — *no header grants anywhere* — for an entirely false reason. 🔵 **The 0-of-9 is only
load-bearing because the instrument demonstrably finds notice when it is present**, which the
**100-of-118**-file `brightspace-mcp-server` row is the positive control for. **A probe that
confirms the prior is the one that most needs one.**

### 🔴 A false-novelty claim this pass made about itself, and withdrew before publishing

🔴 **The first draft of this pass claimed `raw.githubusercontent.com` as a lane "p138 recorded as
closed" and "reopened".** 🟢 **It is neither.** `agents/top.md` already documents it as the working
substitute for the blocked REST API, and **p136's own evidence file used it**. p138's script comment
records only `api.github.com` and `codeload` as unavailable. 🔵 **The defensible claim is narrower
and survives**: p138's probe read only npm, so the payload and repository layers had never been
measured in the **same pass** — which is what makes the AGPL row below a two-layer finding.

# Education — open gaps

**Pass 132, 2026-10-11.** ⏱️ **Nineteenth pass of this date.** 🔴 **This pass's finding is that a gap
can be WRONG rather than merely stale — and the one that was wrong is the one this register had just
promoted to "the largest genuine hole in this KB".**

p131 diagnosed gap *degradation*: a precise gap in this file restated as an absolute absence on a
live page, each error a single quantifier swap. p132 finds the failure one level deeper. **The SIS
agent gap was not degraded in restatement. It was false at the point of measurement, in this file,
and it stayed false for several passes** — because every probe that tested it was built from the
wrong vocabulary.

## 🔴 The defect: a gap measured with the analyst's words about a field named in the builders' words

| this register's gap | how it was probed | why the probe could not work |
|---|---|---|
| *"No AI agent for any system of record"* — 🟢 *"now the largest genuine hole in this KB"* (p131) | `student information system …`, `school management AI agent …`, `SIS …` | 🔴 **The category term does not appear in the field.** The 21 repos that exist are called `librus-mcp`, `edupage-mcp`, `mcp-pronotes`, `iserv-mcp`, `sisu-mcp`, `soongpt-plugin`, `vtop-bhopal-mcp`, `qldt-hanu-mcp`, `mcgill-vsb-mcp`, `nycu`. **None contains "student", "information", "system", "SIS" or "school management"** |

🔵 **This is not `P131-E` and it is worse.** `P131-E` said a multi-term query returns a zero that
measures the query — the fix was fewer terms. **Here the fix is different words entirely.** No star
threshold, no term reduction and no amount of grepping this KB would have found the tier, because
the KB never possessed the vocabulary. p131's remedy (*"grep your own append-only pages before
declaring absence"*) would have returned nothing and confirmed the false gap.

🟢 **The probe that worked, and the generalisable rule.**
`timetable timetabling MCP in:name,description` → **60 results, ~21 education rows.** Timetable
access is **the one capability every member of the field implements**, so it is the only word that
reaches all of them. **Rule, now on `agents/top.md`: before declaring a CLASS absent, probe it three
ways — the category term, the capability every member must implement, and the proper nouns of the
market.** Probe 3 is where *regional* supply hides, and it returns rows with their region already
attached as evidence.

## 🔴 🆕 `P126-C` — `ACTION AJ` and `ACTION AK` are one mechanism, and neither works alone

The 15 violations `ACTION AF` newly surfaced decompose exhaustively, and 🔴 **mis-binding explains
none of them**:

| n | class | why |
|---|---|---|
| **6** | `pupilfirst/pupilfirst` CC-BY-SA-4.0 | 🟢 `AK`'s class — a split grant collapsed to one token, so the surviving member reads as superseded |
| **4** | `oat-sa/tao-core` LGPL-3.0 | unmarked correction apparatus: a quoted retraction, and an old column whose header was not read |
| **3** | `instructure/canvas-lms`, `openedx/edx-platform` `GPL` | 🔴 **SUBSTRING, not binding** |
| **2** | `1EdTech/openbadges-specification` Apache-2.0 | the referent is *"the validator"* — named in prose, not as an address, so binding structurally cannot reach it |

🔴 **The 3 are `ACTION AG`'s own SUBSTRING class recurring in a function `AG` never reached.**
`repair_search.violations` tests `re.escape(tok)` between word boundaries instead of the
vocabulary, and `\bGPL\b` matches inside `GPL-3.0`. Line 524 of `compose/patterns.md` carries no
bare `GPL` at all — the vocabulary reads `GPL-3.0` and `AGPL-3.0`. `AG` guarded token *reading*;
the violation *check* was outside it.

🔴 **And `AK` cannot be implemented without `AJ`.** An address-level survivor set must be fed by
*bound* tokens. `compose/patterns.md` carries one cell naming [`CAHLR/pyBKT`](https://github.com/CAHLR/pyBKT)
and [`douglasrizzo/catsim`](https://github.com/douglasrizzo/catsim) together, giving each its own
token in a parenthetical and retracting the earlier *"both"* reading. An unbound union hands
`MIT`, true of `pyBKT`, to `catsim` as a surviving member — clearing `catsim`'s superseded `MIT` on
**9** live rows: the defect p125 called *the one worth the pass*, re-opened by its own remedy.

🔵 **That cell is described here rather than quoted, and the reason is a finding of its own.**
🔴 **`mark_forms` is not fence-aware**: `_is_quote` skips a fence's delimiter lines but nothing
tracks fence STATE, so a licence token inside a fenced block is read as live prose. Quoting the
cell verbatim — even fenced — registered as an unmarked retraction on **7** pages, and the
self-audit caught it before this commit. `ACTION AR` makes the fence a scope.

| run | `pupilfirst` cleared (wanted 6) | `catsim/MIT` kept (wanted 9) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AK` alone (`--no-bind`) | 🟢 6 | 🔴 **0 — laundered** | 🔴 refuted |
| 🟢 **`AK` over `AJ`** | 🟢 **6** | 🟢 **9** | 🟢 **not refuted** |

🟢 **So `AJ` is refuted as a CAUSE and indispensable as a MECHANISM, and those are not opposites.**
The binder needed three rules in priority order: a **short name** in backticks within 30 characters
(the only rule that resolves the `pyBKT`/`catsim` row — cell and distance both fail); **ordinal
pairing** where k addresses and k tokens sit in two cells; then the **cell wall and nearest
address**. Composed, the assertion falls from **49** violations over 23 addresses to **27** over 13.

## 🔴 🆕 `P125-H` — the assertion that a repair must be corpus-wide was itself run over half the corpus

p124's `ACTION AC` exists to enforce one rule: *a repair must be a SEARCH, not an edit* — for
every repaired `(address, superseded token)`, no page may carry that token on a line naming that
address outside a marked span. p124 discharged it at **27 violations over 15 addresses** and
reported that all 27 were read by hand and **none** was a live false claim.

🔴 **Re-derived independently from p124's own committed code and pages, the assertion returns 61
violations over 23 addresses — 2.3× p124's figure.** The difference is not the recogniser and not
the token vocabulary; both were reproduced exactly. It is the **domain**: run over the five pages
p124 had just marked, the assertion returns **23 violations over 15 addresses** — p124's address
count exactly, and its violation count to within four.

| domain | violations | addresses |
|---|---|---|
| `agents/top.md`, `repos/foundations.md`, `verticals/solutions.md`, `intel/market.md`, `compose/patterns.md` | **23** | **15** — p124 published 27 / 15 |
| 🔴 **all ten live pages** | 🔴 **61** | 🔴 **23** |

🔴 **The five pages it did not reach are `agents/trending.md`, `repos/trending.md`,
`intel/trends.md`, `intel/open-gaps.md` and `README.md` — and the trending pages are where the
largest number of stale tokens live, because they are append-only and a repair is never allowed to
rewrite them.** 🟢 **So the finding is not that p124 was careless; it is that the one instrument
built to prove a repair was corpus-wide had a domain narrower than the corpus, and nothing in the
instrument could say so.** This is p122's `P122-H`, p123's `P123-H` and p124's `P124-H` one level
up: p122 found a census less precise than the page, p123 a repair that was an edit, p124 a token
read without its scope — and p125 finds **an assertion run without its domain**.

🟢 **Every instrument in this lineage now takes its page list from one place and asserts its own
cardinality.** `test_p125.sh` checks the baseline is 61 over ten pages before it scores anything.

## 🟢 `ACTION AF` — one retraction CUE, not thirteen regexes

p124's `ACTION AC` enumerated **nine** surface forms of this KB's correction apparatus and reached
four. p125 began by writing one pattern per unreached form and stopped at **thirteen**:

| # | form | status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `⚠️ **was X**` bold | 🟢 p123 |
| 2 | audit-table OLD column | 🟢 p124 |
| 3 | prose `was X` + publication reference | 🟢 p124 |
| 9 | NEW column named by its SOURCE | 🟢 p124 |
| 4 | `⚠️ *was X*` **italic** | 🟢 **p125** |
| 5 | `⚠️ **KB said X**` | 🟢 **p125** |
| 6 | reversed `(New, published Old)` | 🟢 **p125** |
| 7 | `as X not Y` | 🟢 **p125** |
| 8 | OLD column whose NEW cell holds **no token** | 🟢 **p125** |
| 10 | 🔴 **`⚠️ was X` with NO emphasis at all** — **19 of the 61 violations**, the single largest class | 🟢 **p125** |
| 11 | prose naming a PRIOR PASS's reading (*"`p1040` read Elastic-2.0 …"*, *"an older row on this shelf said AGPL-3 and was superseded"*) | 🟢 **p125** |
| 12 | a `P###-x` finding SECTION whose heading announces the correction | 🟢 **p125** |
| 13 | a licence named in a **CONTRAST clause** (*"Neither restriction exists under AGPL-3"*) | 🟢 **p125 — and it needs no marker at all** |

🟢 **Enumeration is losing, and FORM 13 is why.** Every pass that writes a correction invents a
spelling, and the sweep that chases it ships one pass later — but a licence token inside a
comparison clause was **never a claim about that repository**, so marking it would record a
correction that never happened. The model therefore changes from a form list to the same two-part
rule the rest of this lineage converged on: a **retraction CUE** (a verb or sigil announcing a
superseded value) and a **SCOPE GATE** (`ACTION AG`) that tells a retraction from a contrast, a
quotation or a live claim. Forms 4, 5 and 10 collapse into one pattern with the asterisks optional.

**81 rows marked** across 9 pages; rows carrying the marker **105 → 190**. Applying it twice marks
nothing (asserted). 🟢 **40 of the 61 baseline violations resolved — the clause required 20.**

🔴 **And three defects in `ACTION AF`'s own first application, each found by re-measuring rather
than by inspection:**

| defect | what it did | the rule it became |
|---|---|---|
| a correction table's column mapping **outlived its table** | a header row whose columns `classify_header` cannot read left the PREVIOUS table's mapping in force, and the foundational shelf's **live** licence column was marked superseded on [`1EdTech/openbadges-validator-core`](https://github.com/1EdTech/openbadges-validator-core) | a header row — the one directly above a `\|---\|` separator — always clears the mapping, read or not |
| the marker landed **inside** the emphasis | `⚠️ *was GPL<!--corrected-->*` splits the span the marker is meant to close, so the row read back as unmarked and the assertion re-raised it — 3 rows, all already repaired | the marker moves past any closing `*`/`**` the cue opened |
| `\| \`GPL\` \| 🟢 **GPL-3.0** \|` read as a correction | 20 Moodle-plugin rows marked as repairs that never happened | a bare family token made precise is a **RESOLUTION**, not a correction — `GPL → GPL-3.0` exactly as p124's `ACTION AD` resolved 41 bare `CC` grants without calling one a correction |

🔵 **A fourth was prose, not code**: *"(`⚠️ **was 🟢 MIT**` inside the cell)"* and
*"read *\"⚠️ **was LGPL-3.0**\"*"* are discussion OF the marker. p124 hit the same wall from the
other side — its headline of 94 marked rows differed from a raw `grep`'s 102 by exactly these
lines. The cue's own position now decides: inside backticks or a quotation it is apparatus. 🔵 **The
test keeps the boundary case separate because it is a judgement rather than a rule**: *"The stale
cell's value was **Apache-2.0**"* is apparatus prose *and* a retraction in its own voice, and it
is marked.

## 🟢 `ACTION AG` — the standing check, and three further instances of its own class

The clause: *refuted if the check does not independently reproduce all four known instances.* It
reproduces all four, each driven through the **naive pattern that actually produced the defect**,
because a gate that can only judge its own matches cannot be shown to catch anything:

| instance | pass | naive read | gate's label |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPL-2.0's preamble names the Lesser GPL — *"(Some other Free Software Foundation software is covered by the GNU Lesser General Public License instead.)"* | p122 | `LGPL` | 🟢 `PREAMBLE` |
| EPL-2.0's secondary-licence clause names GPL-2.0 | p123 | `GPL-2.0` | 🟢 `SECONDARY` |
| CC 4.0's own boilerplate names CC0 | p124 | `CC0-1.0` | 🟢 `DOCUMENT-TEXT` |
| `CC BY` matches **inside** `CC BY-SA 4.0` | p124 | a second licence → a split grant | 🟢 `SUBSTRING` |

🔴 **p124's description of its own third instance is wrong, and a gate built to that description
finds nothing.** p124 called it *"the CC 4.0 legalcode **recommends** CC0 in its own
boilerplate"*. The sentence in the file reads *"The text of the Creative Commons public licenses
is dedicated to the public domain under the CC0 Public Domain Dedication."* That is a real grant
with a real verb — and its **subject is the licence document, not the licensed material**. The
label is `DOCUMENT-TEXT`, not `RECOMMENDATION`, and the distinction is the whole content of the
check: the question is never *"is there a verb?"* but *"what does the verb govern?"*

🔴 **Three further instances, none of them hypothesised, all found by the gate's own controls:**

| # | instance | consequence before the gate |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 🔴 **`MIT` matches inside `LIMITED`, and `ISC` inside `DISCLAIMED`** | **every BSD-3 and Apache-2.0 warranty disclaimer on earth** yields a spurious `MIT` grant. The `SUBSTRING` check could not see it — it compares a span against other LICENCE tokens, and `LIMITED` is not one. 🔴 **This was p125's own first build: the fifth instance of the class, committed inside the module written to prevent it** |
| 6 | AGPL-3's **section 13** is a compatibility grant over a work being *combined* with this one — *"permission to link or combine any covered work with a work licensed under version 3 of the GNU General Public License"* | one AGPL-3 file yielded **five** spurious `GPL` grants, enough to make every AGPL-3.0 repository in the corpus read as dual-licensed |
| 7 | AGPL-3's preamble spends a paragraph on the **historical Affero GPL** to say this is *not* it — *"This is a different license, not a version of the Affero GPL"* | two more spurious `GPL` grants from the same file |
| 8 | `ankitects/anki`: *"without the need to license your work under an **AGPL3-compatible license**"* | a compatibility **class** read as a grant (found by `ACTION AH`, below) |

🟢 **The controls assert an EXACT grant set, not non-emptiness** — p124's `ACTION AE` established
that a model scored only where it cannot fail scores perfectly and means nothing, and a control
that only asks *"did it find anything?"* is that same mistake in a test.

## 🟢 `ACTION AH` — `ankitects/anki` is six licences, not two

p124 published [`ankitects/anki`](https://github.com/ankitects/anki) as `AGPL-3.0 + CC-BY-SA` and
recorded the set as **partial**: the per-file exceptions sit in a bulleted list no single binding
window spans. The clause: *refuted if fewer than 3 further tokens are recovered.* **Four are.**

🟢 **A list distributes one introducing sentence over many items, so a binding is assembled from
three levels rather than matched in one window** — the grant verb from *"The following included
source code items use a license other than AGPL3:"*, the directory from *"In the qt folder:"*, and
the artifact and licence from the bullet itself.

| scope | token | read from |
|---|---|---|
| *(whole repository)* | `AGPL-3.0` | *"Anki is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later"* |
| contributed portions | 🆕 **`BSD-3-Clause`** | *"with portions contributed by Anki users licensed under the BSD-3 license (see CONTRIBUTORS)"* |
| `pylib/statsbg.py` | 🆕 **`CC-BY-4.0`** | ` * statsbg.py: CC BY 4.0.` |
| `qt/mpv.py`, `qt/winpaths.py`, `qt/jQuery and jQuery-UI`, `qt/plot.js` | 🆕 **`MIT`** | four bullets |
| `qt/MathJax` | 🆕 **`Apache-2.0`** | ` * MathJax: Apache 2.` |
| `qt/protobuf.js` | `BSD-3-Clause` | ` * protobuf.js: BSD 3 clause` — **no trailing period** |
| `docs-site/` | `CC-BY-SA-4.0` | the file's last paragraph |

🔵 **Three things the list names that are NOT grants over this tree**, and the gate discards each:
*"Binary distributions also include copies of Qt translation files **(LGPL)**"* → `OUT-OF-TREE`;
*"an **AGPL3-compatible** license"* → `SECONDARY`; and *"Anki's translations are **a mix of** BSD
and public domain"* → no single grant for the item, so no binding. 🟢 **`jQuery-UI` is not split at
its own hyphen** — the item separator is a colon or a spaced dash, which cost one fixture to learn.

🔴 **The cause is structural, not carelessness: these pages record licences with per-artifact
precision, and any census that reduces a repository to ONE token is less precise than the text it
audits.** Verified examples the census called defects and which are correct:

|---|---|---|
| `microsoft/autogen` | *"MIT (`LICENSE-CODE`) · `LICENSE` is CC-BY-4.0 for docs"* | both files exist; the scan read `LICENSE` only |

🟢 **The generalisable rule, and `ACTION W`: a census may not publish a defect rate until it has
been scored against rows known to be CORRECT.** An instrument that has never been shown a correct
row it mishandles has not been calibrated, and its rate is a property of the instrument.
🔵 **This is p121's "rate measured on a selected sample" lesson one level up: p121 checked whether
its denominator was honest; p122 had to check whether its detector was.**

| `P122-B2` | EPL-2.0's secondary-licence clause names *"GNU General Public License, version 2.0"*; MPL-2.0 names the GPL and AGPL | `epl2-secondary-names-gpl2.txt`, `mpl2-secondary-names-gpl.txt` |
| `P122-C` | a **split grant** has no single token — `LICENSE` vs `LICENSE-CODE`, code vs docs vs data. Reporting whichever name appears first is arbitrary | `mit-split-grant-names-cc.txt`, `split-unmarked-code-vs-content.txt` |
| `P122-D` | a split marker is **language-specific** — pt-BR *"usa duas licenças"*. An English-only marker list reads a dual licence as a single one | `split-grant-portuguese.txt` |
| `P122-E` | LGPL-3.0 committed **without its title line**, identifiable only by its own incorporation sentence; and the R/CRAN **stub** (`YEAR:` + `COPYRIGHT HOLDER:` only, grant in `DESCRIPTION`) which must never read as "no grant" | `lgpl3-headerless.txt`, `r-stub-licence.txt` |

read correctly.

### 🟢 🆕 `P115-AK` — all five of this KB's python gates failed under the invocation their own READMEs prescribe, and now do not

🔵 **Found while validating this pass's writes against the gates, which is what the gates are
for. The environment's standing instruction is to run python over downloaded or untrusted
input with `python3 -I`, and several of these gates' own READMEs state their suites are
"green under `python3 -I`". Measured:**

| gate | `python3` (plain) | 🔴 `python3 -I` (as documented) |
|---|---|---|
| `p370-gap-gate` | 🟢 **27/27** | 🔴 **`ModuleNotFoundError: test_gap_gate`** |
| `p471-gap-gate-language` | 🟢 **25/25** | 🔴 **`ModuleNotFoundError: test_gap_language`** |
| `p243-frontmatter-coverage` | 🟢 **23/23** | 🔴 **`ModuleNotFoundError: check_frontmatter`** |
| `p239-table-integrity` | 🟢 **OK** | 🔴 **`ModuleNotFoundError: check_tables`** |
| `p383-region-heading-gate` | 🟢 **11/11** | 🔴 **`ModuleNotFoundError: check_headings`** |

🔴 **Five of five. The cause is one line of Python semantics: `-I` is isolated mode and it
drops the SCRIPT'S OWN DIRECTORY from `sys.path`, so every sibling import fails.** 🟢 **The
gates themselves were never broken — their documented invocation was, and `-I` also ignores
`PYTHONPATH`, so the obvious workaround does not work either.**

🔵 **Why it is worth a finding and not a footnote: this is `P471`'s failure wearing a
different hat. `P471` recorded that a gate which cannot parse its input returned the same
verdict as a clean tree — "nothing to judge" where the truth was "I cannot read this". A gate
that cannot be RUN is the same shape one step earlier, and a traceback is only loud while a
human is reading it. Any wrapper that checked an exit code and not the output would have
reported five clean gates.**

🟢 **FIXED, in two lines per file, and verified in both directions:** each gate and each suite
now inserts its own directory at the head of `sys.path`, and all five pass **27/27, 25/25,
23/23, OK, 11/11 under `python3 -I` AND unchanged under plain `python3`** — no regression in
the invocation earlier passes actually used.

|---|---|

| `p370-gap-gate --sweep` | 🟢 **5 declared gaps with a region, none of them this pass's** — and this pass's APAC gap is written in the scoped form p113 was praised for: *"APAC's zero is a property of WHERE this instrument looks, not of the shelf"*, never "the shelf has no APAC rows" |

### 🟡 The rule error the suite caught before the shelf did

🔵 **Recorded because the KB's standard is that an instrument should find its own faults
first.** The first draft of `P114-C` gave a pinned `requirements.txt` the same ancestor
reach as a `package-lock.json`. A root `requirements.txt` pinned with `==` then certified
every unpinned requirements file beneath it — including a `dev/requirements-dev.txt`
reading `black`. The `reqmixed` fixture failed, and the fix (`P114-G`) is the difference
between the two artefacts: **a lockfile is OUTPUT** — a resolver produced it from a
manifest at that directory and, in the workspace ecosystems, enumerates the members it
resolved; **a pinned requirements.txt is INPUT** — a list that pins itself and resolves
nothing below it. Python is the dominant ecosystem on this shelf, so this is the rule
that moved the most rows, and like every other rule in `cover.awk` it can only move them
DOWN.

### 🔴 Six faults in the instrument's own code, each caught against a real payload

🔵 **Published because `p1040` set the precedent: the only honest way to publish a figure
is to publish the bugs it survived.**

1. 🔴 **`FS = "\t"` in `BEGIN`.** The `git cat-file --batch` header is SPACE separated, so
   `$3` was empty, every payload size read as 0, and every content line became a stray.
   Caught by a smoke test written before the suite existed.
2. 🔴 **`P113-M` — the record separator is OPTIONAL.** Git writes one newline after each
   payload: a blank line when the payload ends in a newline, nothing when it does not.
   Consuming it unconditionally ate the next HEADER. 🔴 **`learningequality/kolibri`

### 🔴 Two faults this instrument found in its OWN code before it found any in the shelf

🔵 **Recorded in the `P1028` tradition — an instrument that has not been caught being wrong
has not been tested hard enough.**

| | fault | how it surfaced |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 🔴 **The URL builder hardcoded `https://github.com/$slug`**, so the offline tests could not run at all — every `file://` fixture became a github address. | 🟢 Fixed by resolving a bare `owner/repo` against github.com and using anything with a scheme verbatim. **That fix is what made a 32-test offline suite possible**, so the bug paid for itself. |
| 2 | 🔴 **`P109-D`: age differenced raw timestamps**, making the answer depend on the reference time of day and the commit's own timezone — a commit nine calendar days back reported as **eight**. | 🟢 Caught by a boundary test, not by inspection. Both sides are now floored to a UTC date first. |

🔵 **A third, in the test harness rather than the instrument: `local n=$1 … r="$T/$n"`
expands every word before assigning any, so `$n` was unset under `set -u`. Recorded because
it silently turned 18 real assertions into false failures.**

### 🔴 Three regressions in this instrument's OWN code, found by DIFFING TWO CENSUS RUNS

🔵 **Not by inspection. The first run used the ECL wiring alone; the second added the five
mechanisms above; `census-diff.2026-10-10.txt` compares them row by row. 43 rows changed family and
three of those changes were WRONG.**

1. 🔴 **`Community License` swallowed ECL.** `"Educational Community License"` **contains** the
   substring the bespoke-terms branch matches, so the non-grant branch took the exact permissive
   family this instrument exists to recover: **10 rows moved to `NON-GRANT`.** 🔴 **The `Gap 398`
   fix inverted into a worse error than the one it repaired**, and only the diff showed it.
2. 🔴 **A copyright formula demoted three Apache-2.0 rows.** `huggingface/transformers`,
   `mlflow/mlflow`, `masakhane-io/masakhane-ner` carry a conventional `All rights reserved` line
   above a full Apache-2.0 text. 🟢 **That branch is GONE: it is a copyright formula, not a
   restriction, and it appears inside BSD notices, which ARE grants.**
3. 🔴 **MPL-2.0 read as GPL-3.0.** MPL section 3.3 **names** the GNU GPL, LGPL and AGPL as
   *"Secondary Licenses"*, so 15 921 B of plain MPL ([`dequelabs/axe-core`](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core))
   matched the case-folded GNU branch.

🟢 **Each is now a test against the payload that produced it** — `fixtures/` carries the three real
texts, not synthetic approximations. 🔵 **And the fix for (1) and (2) needed a THIRD attempt, which
is `P1042`: the ECL title appears five times in the Sakai payload and the fifth WRAPS as
`Licensed under the Educational\nCommunity License`. A strip keyed on the unwrapped title removed
four of five and left a bare `Community License` at the start of line 196 — ECL came back a conflict
again, from ONE LINE BREAK.**

### 🔴 And two in its own PLUMBING — a silence counted as data, twice

🔴 **`probe_one` runs inside an `xargs bash -c` subshell, so every function it calls must be named
in `export -f`. Twice this pass one was not.**

- 🔴 **First: `classify_restricted` was unexported. Its "command not found" went to stderr while the
  census wrote a row for every address anyway** — empty output fell through `classify_grant`'s final
  case and **1 077 rows published a BLANK licence that tallied as `UNREAD`.** 🔵 **The `Gap 398`
  failure mode in its purest form — a silence counted as data — produced by plumbing, not by any
  licence text.**
- 🔴 **Second: the guard added to catch exactly that MISSED IT**, because the guard kept its own copy
  of the same list and `declares_known_grant` was in neither. 🔴 **2 162 stderr lines, 1 381 rows
  emitted.**

🟢 **Fixed at the root (`P1044`): the export list is DERIVED from `classify.sh` — every top-level
`name()` definition — and the guard iterates the derived list and REFUSES to emit rows when any
function is invisible to a child shell.** 🔵 **Verified by removing an export:
`REFUSING TO RUN: classify_payload is defined but not exported to the worker subshell`, exit 2.**

🟢 **`raw.githubusercontent.com` serves the literal ref `HEAD`**, so `p1029`'s per-address
`git ls-remote --symref` — spent purely to learn a default branch name — is unnecessary.
🔵 **And the case that would break a guessed branch name is real: `sakaiproject/sakai` answers
**200 at `HEAD`** and **404 at `main`**, because its default is `master`.** 🟢 **99 addresses in 13 s;

### 🔵 Principles adopted: `P1040`–`P1047`

- **`P1040`** — 🔴 **a remedy that lives BESIDE the instrument is not a remedy.** `classify_ecl` was
  written in pass 105 and ran on four addresses; wired into the census it recovered **10**.
  🟢 **The gap closes when the remedy is in the code path the next count will take, not when it is
  written.**
- **`P1041`** — 🔴 **a restriction branch must never fire unchallenged on a payload that DECLARES a
  known grant family.** Where both are genuinely present the answer is not a silent pick either way
  but `GRANT+RESTRICTION-CONFLICT`, bucketed for a hand-read (`caviraoss/pagelm`: an MIT grant plus
  7.5 KB of further terms). 🔵 **Silent promotion is a legal problem; silent demotion cost three
  Apache-2.0 rows.**
- **`P1042`** — 🔴 **match licence text on FLATTENED whitespace.** Licence files are hard-wrapped at
  ~72 columns, so any multi-word pattern can straddle a newline. 🟢 **The ECL title wraps at line
  195 of the Sakai payload and defeated a strip keyed on the unwrapped form.**
- **`P1043`** — 🔴 **a licence that REFERENCES another family must be settled BEFORE the family it
  references.** MPL-2.0 names the GPL/LGPL/AGPL as Secondary Licenses. 🔵 **The same hazard
  `classify_payload` already documents for AFFERO-before-GPL, one level up — and it reached a real
  row.**
- **`P1044`** — 🔴 **a guard keyed on a hand-maintained list fails in exactly the case it exists
  for.** The export guard and the export line kept separate copies of one list, and the function
  added to neither went undetected. 🟢 **Derive the list from the source file.**
- **`P1045`** — 🔴 **the copyright line INSIDE a copyleft payload is the LICENCE's copyright, not
  the PROJECT's.** Reading it as the holder puts the Free Software Foundation, of Boston, behind
  every GPL and AGPL row in the corpus. 🟢 **Read the holder from `NOTICE`, the README or the
  manifest; `P1035`'s placing discipline is worthless on a field that names the wrong party.**
- **`P1046`** — 🔴 **a declared-licence field is free text.** `GPL-3.0-or-later` (136), `GPL-3.0+`
  (5) and `GPLv3` (2) are three spellings of one grant; a census keyed on an exact string splits the
  dominant family into three buckets and reports none of them as dominant. 🔵 **`P1037` reaching the
  DECLARED field.**
- **`P1047`** — 🟢 **a sample understates a blind spot in proportion to how CLUSTERED the blind
  family is.** ECL was 2 of 99 sampled and 10 of 1 381 held, because it clusters in one consortium's
  repositories rather than spreading evenly. 🔵 **So a blindness measured on a sample gives a floor,
  never an estimate.**

### 🔴 `Gap 398` OPENED — ECL-2.0 is **invisible** to this KB's licence classifier, and the permissive count was wrong

🔵 **Pass 90 said "ECL-2.0 is why six passes undercounted the permissive platform tier."**
🔴 **That was a diagnosis. This pass measured the mechanism, and the mechanism is worse than the
diagnosis, because it is still running.**

🟢 **`classify_payload` — the classifier `p1029` ran over all 99 addresses in pass 104 — returns
`UNRECOGNISED` for all six live Apereo-lineage ECL payloads.** 🔵 **Measured cause, not inferred:
the real ECL-2.0 text contains ZERO occurrences of the string `Apache License`.** It names the
*"Apache 2.0 license"* in lower case, so a classifier keyed on the Apache title never fires.

🟡 **This pass predicted the opposite.** `test_p1035.sh` was written asserting that ECL would
**mislabel as Apache-2.0**; the live payloads refuted the assertion, and the test now encodes the
measured behaviour with both branches kept:

| failure mode | what it does to a census |
|---|---|
| `MISLABEL-AS-APACHE` | 🟡 a wrong grant, but a *permissive* one — the row still counts |
| 🔴 **`INVISIBLE-TO-CENSUS`** — what actually happens | 🔴 **a permissive row lands in NEITHER the permissive nor the copyleft bucket** |

🔴 **And the bucket DEFINITION compounds the classifier.** Pass 104 published
*"permissive (MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD)"* — a name with no room for ECL in it. 🟢 **Both corrected,
and the 68 granted rows now reconcile to the last row:**

| bucket | pass 104 | 🟢 **corrected** | the difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| permissive | 38 | 🟢 **40** | 🔴 **`lap-sakai-extractor` + `opendashboard-legacy`, both ECL-2.0, both permissive, both uncounted** |
| copyleft | 22 | 22 | `openmage/magento-lts` (10 293 B) read as **OSL-3.0** — pass 104 had this one right |
| CC family | 5 | 5 | — |
| 🔴 payload that is **not a grant** | 1 | 1 | `yuanjiusheng/cloud-learning-ce`, 4 117 B of all-rights-reserved (`P1029`) |
| **total granted** | 68 | **68** | 🟢 **40 + 22 + 5 + 1 = 68. It reconciles.** |

🔵 **So `UNRECOGNISED` was never one thing.** It held a permissive grant the classifier cannot see,
a copyleft grant it happens to have named elsewhere, and a genuine non-grant — 🟢 **three different
facts behind one label, separable only by reading the payload.**

### 🔵 Principles adopted: `P1029`–`P1034`

- **`P1029`** — 🔴 **a `LICENSE` that returns 200 is not a grant.**
  [`yuanjiusheng/cloud-learning-ce`](https://github.com/yuanjiusheng/cloud-learning-ce) serves
  4 117 B of all-rights-reserved Chinese copyright assertion from a file named `LICENSE`
  (*「保留所有权利」*). 🟢 **It classifies `UNRECOGNISED` because it matches no grant; a
  filename→licence mapping would have shelved a proprietary LMS as open source.**
- **`P1030`** — 🔴 **a payload ABOVE its family's pristine size can be a SECOND LICENCE, not a
  bundled notice.** `magnusvron/llm-benchmark-quality-index` is **2 488 B** against MIT's ~1 070 B
  and is dual-licensed (MIT for code, separate terms for data). 🔵 **`P1024` read an above-pristine
  excess as someone else's bundled grant; this is the other cause, and only reading the payload
  separates them.** 🟢 **Found by a spread check: 28 of 29 MIT rows fall in 1 058–1 152 B.**
- **`P1031`** — 🔴 **inside one org name, the grant tracks the HOLDER, not the org.**
  `nextcloud/llm2`, `translate2`, `text2image_stablediffusion2` are **MIT held by `cloud-py-api`**;
  `integration_openai` and `context_chat_backend` are **AGPL-3.0**. 🟢 **Model runners embeddable,
  integration layer network-copyleft; the org name says neither.** 🔵 **`P1012` in the permissive
  direction.**
- **`P1032`** — 🔴 **a fork inherits the CONTENT and not necessarily the GRANT.** Three forks of
  `awesome-eu-ai-act`: `genai-gurus` and `mlx-cassio` carry CC0 at **7 049 B with the identical
  `sha256` `7179683e8000e6bd`** 🟢 *(`P1025` satisfied, not merely suggested)*; `morganrcu` carries
  **no payload at all**.
- **`P1034`** — 🔴 **a new instrument's INPUT files enter the corpus an existing instrument
  measures, and can silently disable it.** `p1029`'s 99-address input list, committed live, would
  have made `p1026`'s census report a loss of **zero** — 🔵 **`p1026`'s own trap, re-entered from
  outside through a different instrument.** 🟢 **Fixed with no edit to `p1026`: its guard excludes
  by FILENAME, so this pass's address lists were NAMED into the patterns it already catches
  (`lost-addresses.*.txt`, `held-only-in-a-worklist.*.txt`, `result.*.tsv`).** 🔵 **`P1026`'s "a
  worklist is not a shelf" gains a second edge: a worklist must not be able to PASS for one.**
- **`P1033`** — 🟢 **the copyleft boundary is the PLUGIN TREE, and it is one HTTP request wide.**
  Probing for a root `version.php`: `jeanlucio/moodle-local_aihub` **200** → GPL-3.0;
  `a2br/moodle-mcp` **404** → MIT; `sngdtechnologies/ai-moodle-security` **404** → BSD-2-Clause.
  🔵 **Code loaded inside the LMS inherits its licence; code speaking across its API, or wrapping it
  in infrastructure, does not.** 🔴 **7 of 7 granted Moodle-plugin rows are GPL-3.0, Microsoft's own
  `o365-moodle` (695 tags) included.**

🔴 **Pass 91's `grant-ladder-v3` wrote its own 30-line classifier instead of sourcing the hardened shared
`compose/code/lib/license_family.sh`. `P237` exists to forbid exactly that, and `lib`'s own header records
that pass 77 had already done it once.** Two platform rows came out with the wrong licence family:

| [`portabilis/i-educar`](https://github.com/portabilis/i-educar) | 🔴 `LGPL-3.0` · 18 092 B · *"link, don't absorb"* | 🔴 **Version 2, June 1991** → **GPL-2.0** |

🔴 **Mechanism — `P171` on a pair `P171` never covered.** The canonical GPL-2.0 **preamble** reads
*"(Some other Free Software Foundation software is covered by the **GNU Lesser General Public License**
instead.)"* at **byte 847** (`tao-core`) and **byte 849** (`i-educar`), inside the 4 000 B window, and the
fork tested `"gnu lesser"` **before** `"gnu general public"`. **Every canonical GPL-2.0 payload carries
that sentence, so the defect was universal rather than incidental.**

🟢 **Control, in the same verdict class and the same run:** `francoisjacquet/rosariosis` is also GPL-2.0 but
its 15 214 B variant has **no `"gnu lesser"` at all** (offset `-1`), so the same classifier returned bare
`GPL`. 🔵 **One instrument, one pass, one family, two verdicts — decided by whether a cross-reference
sentence happened to be present.**

🔴 **THE COST WAS NOT INTERNAL, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS THE PASS'S HEADLINE.** `verticals/solutions.md`
recommended by name *"a **Brazilian public-sector SIS** → `i-educar` (**LGPL-3.0**) — **link, don't
absorb**"*, and `compose/patterns.md` built `P91-E` on *"LGPL-3.0 permits exactly that, and **this
distinction makes the engagement possible**"*. **"Link, don't absorb" is advice that exists only for LGPL.**
🟢 All three files corrected; `P91-E` re-costed around a service boundary with the cost increase stated.

🔵 **And this KB already knew both answers.** `repos/trending.md` published *"the row that decides a
project: `oat-sa/tao-core` is GPL-2.0"* — derived, in its own words, *"by reusing the shared classifier
`lib/license_family.sh` (`P237`) instead of rewriting it"*. `agents/trending.md` carried
`| portabilis/i-educar | LGPL | 🔴 GPL-2.0 | LATAM |`. 🔴 **The corrections existed and a new instrument
overwrote them.**

🟢 **`P960` adopted: a licence body names other families in order to relate itself to them — GPL-3.0 §13 →
Affero, GPL-2.0 preamble → Lesser, MPL-2.0 §1.12 → three GNU marks, EUPL's Appendix → five families. The
identity lives in the TITLE BLOCK and nowhere else.** Generalises `P171` and `P453`/`P454`.
🟢 **`P963` adopted: a shelf row's licence may only be re-derived by an instrument at least as hardened as
the one that last published it. An instrument-quality regression silently overwrites verified values.**
